brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine the optimal frequency, duration, and timing of physical therapy (PT) and occupational therapy (OT) rehabilitation to improve physical and cognitive function in critically ill adults receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. What combination of rehabilitation session frequency, session duration, and timing of OT initiation produces the greatest improvements in physical function and activities of daily living at hospital discharge and 3 months?
2. Which patient characteristics, including age and comorbidities, are associated with greater benefits from different rehabilitation approaches?

Researchers will compare eight combinations of rehabilitation strategies, varying three components:

Session frequency: 4 versus 7 days per week. Session duration: 20 versus 40 minutes per session. Timing of OT initiation: Early initiation (within 24 hours of randomization) versus delayed initiation (at ICU discharge or 7 days after randomization, whichever occurs later).

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of eight rehabilitation combinations.
* Receive individualized, progressive PT focused on strength, balance, mobility, and endurance, beginning within 24 hours of randomization.
* Receive individualized OT focused on daily activities, including grooming, bathing, dressing, and feeding, beginning according to their assigned group.
* Participate in rehabilitation sessions until hospital discharge, 21 days after randomization, or successful completion of predefined rehabilitation milestones, whichever occurs first.
* Undergo assessments of physical function, daily activities, and cognitive function during hospitalization and at hospital discharge.
* Complete a follow-up assessment 3 months after hospital discharge to evaluate physical and cognitive function, quality of life, mental health, and recovery.
primary_outcomes: Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) Score
Activity Measure for Post-Acute Care (AM-PAC) Daily Activity Score
title: Optimizing Acute Care Rehabilitation for Critically Ill Adults

brief_summary:
This study is a research proposal designed to evaluate the effect of non-pharmacological interventions-specifically stress ball application and listening to music-on intraoperative anxiety, surgical fear, and the feeling of safety in patients undergoing trigger finger (stenosing tenosynovitis) surgery under local anesthesia.

Key Summary Highlights Trigger Finger Condition \& Treatment: Trigger finger is a mechanical restriction caused by the thickening of flexor tendons and their sheaths, leading to painful locking at the metacarpophalangeal joint. When conservative treatments (e.g., physical therapy, splints, corticosteroid injections) prove ineffective, open surgical release is the definitive treatment with high success rates.

Local Anesthesia \& Intraoperative Stressors: Performing day-surgery procedures under local anesthesia offers quick recovery, but preserving consciousness exposes patients to stressful sensory stimuli-such as loud orthopedic surgical tools, technical staff conversations, and physical sensations of pulling or pressure. This frequently triggers loss of control, high intraoperative anxiety, and surgical fear, which can activate the sympathetic nervous system and impair vital signs and overall satisfaction.

Non-Pharmacological Nursing Interventions:

Music Therapy: Acts through neurophysiological mechanisms by regulating brainwave frequencies and neurochemical activity, promoting muscle relaxation, reducing stress, and inducing an anxiolytic effect.

Stress Ball Application: Rhythmic hand squeezing reduces muscular tension, provides emotional relaxation, and diverts attention away from surgical stressors.

H1₁: Stress ball application during trigger finger surgery performed under local anesthesia has an effect on anxiety level.

Aim of the Study The aim of this study is to determine the effect of stress ball application and listening to music during trigger finger surgery performed under local anesthesia on anxiety, surgical fear, and feeling of safety, thereby contributing high-level evidence to non-invasive intraoperative nursing care.

brief_summary:
Surgery to remove the head of the pancreas (pancreatoduodenectomy, also called the Whipple operation), usually followed by chemotherapy, is the only treatment that offers long-term survival for cancer in the head of the pancreas (pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma). Even so, the cancer comes back (recurs) in most patients. Where it comes back first (around the operation site, in the liver, in the lining of the abdomen, in the lungs or elsewhere) and how soon it comes back both affect survival, the choice of further treatment and how patients should be followed up.

CA 19-9 is a blood test measured routinely before this operation. A high level is known to be linked with shorter survival, but whether it also predicts where and when the cancer will recur is uncertain and, to the investigator's knowledge, has not been studied in patients treated in Egypt. Jaundice, which is common in these patients, can raise CA 19-9 falsely, so this study uses only CA 19-9 values measured when the blood bilirubin level was close to normal (2 mg/dL or less).

This is a retrospective study of existing medical records. It includes adults who had a Whipple operation for this cancer at the Hepatopancreatobiliary and Surgical Oncology Unit, Liver and GIT Hospital, Minia University, Egypt, between January 2017 and December 2024, with follow-up information from Minia Oncology Centre. No patient will receive any test or treatment for the study, and no care will be changed. Patients will be compared according to their preoperative CA 19-9 level (37 U/mL or less versus more than 37 U/mL).

The two main questions are whether the preoperative CA 19-9 level is linked to (1) the site of the first recurrence and (2) the time from surgery to recurrence. A recurrence will count only when confirmed by scans or biopsy, never by a rising CA 19-9 alone, and it will be classified by independent doctors who do not know the patients' CA 19-9 results. Other questions include recurrence within 6 and 12 months of surgery, survival, and whether CA 19-9 adds useful information to the routine findings available before surgery.

The investigator expects that patients with a high CA 19-9 will more often recur first in the liver or the lining of the abdomen and will recur sooner, whereas patients with a normal level will recur later and more often only near the operation site. The findings may help tailor follow-up after surgery, identify patients who might benefit from chemotherapy before surgery, and identify patients whose cancer is likely to come back only at the operation site, who might be considered for further local treatment.
primary_outcomes: Anatomical pattern of first recurrence, by index preoperative CA 19-9 group (>37 vs ≤37 U/mL)
Time to first recurrence, with death without recurrence as a competing event, by index preoperative CA 19-9 group
title: Preoperative CA 19-9 and the Pattern and Timing of Recurrence After Pancreatoduodenectomy (Whipple Operation) for Pancreatic Cancer

The objective of this study was to compare the clinical effects of hyaluronic acid (HA) and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) as adjuncts to the tunnel surgical technique in the management of Miller Class I (RT1) gingival recession defects in the esthetic zone among systemically healthy patients.

A total of 30 systemically healthy patients presenting with RT1 gingival recession defects were randomly allocated into three groups, with 10 patients in each group. All patients underwent surgical treatment using the tunnel technique. In the first group, 0.2% hyaluronic acid gel (Gengigel®) was applied to the exposed root surface and within the prepared tunnel. In the second group, the exposed root surface was conditioned with 24% EDTA for 2 minutes, followed by saline irrigation. The third group received the tunnel technique alone and served as the control group.

Clinical outcomes were evaluated at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months postoperatively. The assessed clinical parameters included recession depth (RD), clinical attachment level (CAL), keratinized tissue width (KTW), probing depth (PD), plaque index (PI), and gingival index (GI), to evaluate changes in periodontal clinical conditions following treatment.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of root coverage assessed using a periodontal probe
title: Comparison of Hyaluronic Acid Versus EDTA as Adjunctive Therapy to Tunnel Technique for Gingival Recession.

brief_summary:
An ACL rupture and reconstruction may be responsible for a neurophysiological dysfunction commonly known as 'arthrogenic muscle inhibition' (AMI). AMI is responsible for the quadriceps deficits observed following an ACL rupture and thus appears to be a major limiting factor in the patient's rehabilitation and functional recovery.

ACL reconstruction is performed under general or regional anaesthesia. A tourniquet may be applied to the thigh to prevent bleeding, but new arthroscopy systems, such as the STRYKER arthroscopy system, allow the surgeon to work within the joint without a tourniquet. This makes it possible to avoid the potential complications associated with the tourniquet, the compression from which can slow down the crural nerve and the sciatic nerve and affect the thigh muscles - in particular the quadriceps, which is involved in AMI - as well as the mobility of the lower limb.

This study is based on the hypothesis that patients undergoing ACL reconstruction without a tourniquet using the STRYKER arthroscopy system experience less quadriceps muscle damage.

Little data is available on this approach in France. This is why this study has been initiated.
primary_outcomes: arthrogenic muscular inhibition (AMI)
title: Assessment of a Tourniquet-free Surgical Reconstruction of the ACL Using the STRYKER Arthroscopy System With Regard to the Occurrence of Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition (AMI) - an Exploratory Study

Catheter-related bladder discomfort (CRBD) is a frequent postoperative complication associated with urinary catheterization. The purpose of this prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was to compare intravenous atropine, hyoscine N-butylbromide, and placebo for the prevention of CRBD in adults undergoing transurethral resection of the prostate or bladder tumors under general anesthesia.

The study interventions consisted of intravenous atropine 0.015 mg/kg, hyoscine N-butylbromide 20 mg, or an equivalent volume of 0.9% sodium chloride solution, administered approximately 10 minutes before completion of surgery.

The primary outcome was the presence of CRBD at one or more scheduled assessments at 1, 6, 12, and 24 hours after surgery. Secondary outcomes included CRBD severity assessed using a four-point categorical scale, postoperative pain intensity assessed using a 100-mm visual analogue scale, rescue analgesic and antiemetic requirements, and adverse effects assessed through clinical observation and participant report.
primary_outcomes: Severity of Catheter-Related Bladder Discomfort (CRBD) Assessed Using a Four-Point CRBD Severity Scale

brief_summary:
Adult spinal deformity (ASD) significantly impacts quality of life through chronic low back pain and/or spinal imbalance, impairing the ability to walk independently in patients both with and without spinal cord injury (SCI). In particular, the importance of sagittal balance of the spine and its correlation with outcome in the bipedal population are well established. Despite extensive efforts to integrate knowledge about sagittal parameters of the spine into surgical planning, there are still debates on which set of biomechanical parameters should be focused on to achieve the optimal surgical result for the individual patient.

Unique IDentifier (UniD) Adaptive Spine Intelligence (ASI, Medtronic) makes spine surgery predictable and repeatable using artificial intelligence - backed by data science. Pre-operative planning with the integration of artificial intelligence mitigates the risk of surgical and realignment failure as well as revision surgery. Once the surgical plan has been decided on, the achievement of the surgical goal is directly related to surgical performance. Here, the placement of screws into the vertebral bodies is one of the main surgical steps in ASD surgery. Thanks to technical developments, the process of screw placement has advanced from conventional X-ray-guided and/or freehand techniques to navigated and robot-assisted techniques. In particular, the safety and reproducibility of screw placement have been claimed to be superior when using robotic assistance.

In the present investigation, the primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility of software-based planning using the UniD ASI software in conjunction with robotic assistance and prebent rods during ASD surgeries with a focus on minimally invasive strategies for deformity correction. The secondary objective is to investigate both patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and patient-reported experience measures (PREMs). The hypothesis is that both software planning with the integration of artificial intelligence and robot-assisted minimally invasive surgeries provide a safe, reproducible, and significant improvement in clinical outcome in ASD patients.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of robotic / artifical intelligence (AI)-assisted surgery
title: Robotic Surgery in Adult Spine Deformity

This study is designed to investigate the impact of a patient specific physiotherapy prehabilitation programme on the outcomes of patients presenting with symptomatic hip dysplasia.

Prehabilitation for peri-acetabular osteotomy (PAO) surgery has not previously been investigated and we do not know the effect it would have on the post-surgical outcomes.

A clinical study is required to investigate the impact formal prehabilitation has on patients undergoing PAO. The investigators will carry out a pilot project to ensure the investigators have the right study design with appropriate outcomes, and that children and families will consent to taking part.

The pilot project will be funded by The Children's Hospital Charity (TCHC). Once successfully completed, the investigators will apply for funding for a large scale, multicentre trial.

Following completion of our research project the investigators will be able to advise patients on the expected effect of prehabilitation on the outcomes of this surgery.

The investigators hypothesise that patients who have a period of prehabilitation prior to surgery will have better physical outcome measures and hip outcome scores compared to those who do not have prehabilitation.

brief_summary:
Alcohol and other drug (AOD) use disorders are associated with a range of adverse outcomes. Relapse following AOD treatment is common. Attendance at Mutual Aid Groups (MAGs) is associated with improved health outcomes and reduced healthcare utilisation costs. National guidance recommends that clinical staff promote MAG attendance, but few patients are referred to, or attend, MAGs. An intensive referral intervention, developed in the United States of America has been shown to increase engagement with MAGs. The aim of this National Institute for Health Research (NIHR)-funded study is to adapt and test a Facilitated Access to Mutual Aid (FAMA) intervention and staff training for delivery in community AOD services in England.

Phase one of this study consists of qualitative focus groups conducted with staff of community AOD services and adults receiving AOD treatment. Eight focus groups will explore participants' views of MAGs and the existing American FAMA intervention. The FAMA intervention will then be adapted and staff training developed, based on the focus group findings and input from patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) groups.

Phase two of this study consists of testing the adapted FAMA intervention. Staff in one community AOD service will receive the newly developed FAMA training. They will deliver FAMA to people who are currently receiving AOD treatment service. Each session will be recorded and the fidelity of intervention delivery will be assessed by the research team using a checklist. Staff and patient feedback will be collected using brief questionnaires in informal feedback sessions. The FAMA intervention will be refined and delivered again with another round of feedback being collected. A final version of the FAMA intervention will then be agreed by the research team and PPIE groups.
primary_outcomes: Qualitative focus groups
Acceptability of Intervention measure (AIM) adapted for FAMA
Feasibility of Intervention (FIM) adapted for FAMA
Appropriateness Measure (IAM) adapted for FAMA
title: Adaptation of Facilitated Access to Mutual Aid for Community Alcohol and Drug Services

brief_summary:
Regional citrate anticoagulation is commonly used during continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) in critically ill patients. Citrate prevents clotting in the extracorporeal circuit by reducing ionized calcium concentrations. However, adequate anticoagulation is not always achieved, and the influence of dialysis and hemofiltration on citrate removal and post-filter ionized calcium remains incompletely understood.

This prospective, single-center, interventional study compares two strategies for increasing extracorporeal clearance in critically ill patients receiving CKRT with regional citrate anticoagulation.

Patients with post-filter ionized calcium concentrations above 0.35 mmol/L two hours after treatment initiation are randomized to either an increase in dialysate flow of 1,000 mL/h or an increase in hemofiltration flow of 1,000 mL/h.

The study evaluates the effects of these two interventions on citrate clearance and post-filter ionized calcium concentrations, with the aim of improving understanding of citrate handling during CKRT.
primary_outcomes: Decrease in Ionized Calcium Across the Hemofilter
title: Effect of Increased Dialysis Versus Hemofiltration

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How do clinical symptoms, cognitive function, body composition and blood biomarkers change during the first 12 months after starting the treatment?
* Are there differences in outcomes between participants treated with DBS and those treated with foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion?

Participants will:

* Undergo deep brain stimulation (DBS) or start continuous subcutaneous foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion as part of their routine clinical care.
* Attend study visits over 12 months and complete assessments of motor and non-motor symptoms, cognition, gait and balance.
* Provide blood samples and undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and body composition measurements.
primary_outcomes: Change in UPDRS Part III (Motor Examination) score
title: Impact of Advanced Parkinson Therapies on Clinical Status: Deep Brain Stimulation and Foslevodopa/Foscarbidopa

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled Phase III clinical study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of LP-003 injection in patients with chronic spontaneous urticaria who remain symptomatic despite treatment with H1 antihistamines.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in weekly Urticaria Activity Score (UAS7) at week 12
title: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of LP-003 Injection in Patients With Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria Who Remain Symptomatic Despite Treatment With H1 Antihistamines

brief_summary: A randomized controlled trial that is trying to find the best treatment for a severe upper leg (i.e., thigh, also known as femoral shaft) fracture. One type of treatment, which is called micromotion intramedullary (within the hollow center of the bone) nailing, is a type of nail used for thigh fracture treatments that helps to heal the bone by allowing a small amount of controlled movement. Another type, called non-micromotion intramedullary nailing, is also used to treat thigh fractures but does not include this controlled-movement feature. Both treatments are approved by the FDA but have not been directly compared to each other. Participation includes being assigned to receive either a micromotion intramedullary nail or a non-micromotion intramedullary nail. Those that participate will be randomly assigned (like a flip of a coin) to one of those treatment methods and return for standard follow-up visits. In addition to those regular clinical follow-ups, participants will complete some brief surveys/questionnaires while they are in the hospital. Research staff will also look at past medical history.
primary_outcomes: Superiority of micromotion nailing over non-micromotion IMN according to a composite outcome using a win ratio reflective of improved femoral shaft fracture healing
title: Intramedullary Nailing for Femoral Shaft Fractures

brief_summary:
Pregnancy-related anxiety is a common concern during pregnancy and may affect maternal well-being. This study aims to evaluate the effect of the NUR (Neuro-Understanding-Relaxation) Prenatal Exercise program on pregnancy-related anxiety among pregnant women.

The study uses a quasi-experimental design with an intervention group and a control group. Pregnant women in the intervention group receive the NUR Prenatal Exercise program, which combines prenatal exercise with structured educational, relaxation, and psychospiritual components. The program consists of eight sessions delivered once a week over eight weeks, with each session lasting approximately 60 minutes.

The control group receives conventional prenatal exercise without the additional structured educational, relaxation, and psychospiritual components.

Pregnancy-related anxiety is assessed using the Pregnancy-Related Anxiety Questionnaire-Revised 2 (PRAQ-R2). Anxiety scores are compared between the intervention and control groups to determine whether the NUR Prenatal Exercise program helps reduce pregnancy-related anxiety.

The findings are expected to provide evidence on the potential role of an integrated prenatal exercise program in supporting maternal psychological well-being during pregnancy.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pregnancy-Related Anxiety Score
title: NUR Prenatal Exercise for Pregnancy-Related Anxiety

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate whether twelve weeks of daily coffee consumption can improve blood vessel elasticity (arterial stiffness) in adults typical of the UK population who are currently non-habitual coffee consumers. Additionally, the effects on cardiometabolic disease risk markers, liver health markers, cognitive function and inter-individual genetic variations in response to coffee consumption will be examined.
primary_outcomes: Cardio-ankle vascular index
title: Coffee and Arterial Stiffness Evaluation

brief_summary:
Project background: SUCCINCT The Structured Utilization of Continence Care Innovations in Nursing Care Trial (SUCCINCT) is a health-oriented, pragmatic implementation study designed to improve continence care in nursing homes. It forms part of the wider European Union (EU)-funded ProCon project, which aims to promote continence through innovation, training, and entrepreneurship in nursing home settings. SUCCINCT addresses a major quality-of-care challenge: urinary and fecal incontinence are highly prevalent among nursing home residents, yet continence care is often limited by insufficient staff knowledge, lack of systematic assessment, poor communication, and over-reliance on containment products rather than individualized care.

Main objectives The primary objective is to determine whether an intervention derived from a novel educational course in continence care for nursing home staff can improve the delivery of continence care and resident satisfaction with continence care. The secondary objective is to assess whether the intervention improves staff workflow, work engagement, and empowerment.

More broadly, the study seeks to understand whether education, facilitation, local leadership, and team-based quality improvement can support sustainable improvements in continence care within complex nursing home environments.

Anticipated study design SUCCINCT will use a pragmatic, quasi-experimental before-after design, comparing intervention units with usual-care units. The study will be conducted across four sites: Alberta (Canada), Barcelona (Spain), Leuven (Belgium), and Turku (Finland). Up to 160 nursing home residents will be recruited, with approximately 40 residents per site: 20 in the intervention group and 20 in the usual-care group. Each country will include one intervention and one usual-care site, preferably in separate homes or organizationally distinct units.

Intervention unit staff will complete ProCon continence education courses, including basic and advanced components. Continence Champions and care teams will then work with SUCCINCT researchers to co-design a locally appropriate continence care intervention. Implementation will occur over 12 weeks and will include facilitation, coaching, team-building, communication support, local measurement, feedback, and Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles. A parallel process evaluation will examine implementation, mechanisms of impact, feasibility, acceptability, fidelity, adaptation, and contextual factors through staff focus group discussions.

Deliverables Key deliverables will include locally tailored continence care interventions for participating nursing home units; trained Continence Champions and care teams; baseline and post-intervention datasets on resident, staff, and system outcomes; process evaluation findings; and practical knowledge on how education and facilitation can support continence care improvement. The study will also generate evidence on the feasibility of implementing ProCon training and related quality improvement activities across diverse international nursing home contexts.

Anticipated results Resident-level outcomes include improved bladder and bowel continence status, fewer urinary incontinence episodes over 24 hours, fewer fecal incontinence episodes per week, and improved satisfaction with continence care, including dignity, autonomy, acceptability, efficiency, and whether care meets residents' needs. Staff-level outcomes include improved work engagement, reduced rushed or missed care tasks, perceived effectiveness of the intervention, enhanced capacity to provide person-centered and dignity-preserving care, and changes in care burden. System-level outcomes include change in the average number of absorbent products used per resident over 24 hours.

Knowledge dissemination and implementation plan Knowledge dissemination will be embedded throughout the project. At the unit level, teams will use feedback from locally collected data to guide iterative improvement during Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles. Continence Champions, senior leaders, and SUCCINCT researchers will support implementation, problem-solving, and adaptation to local context. Findings from quantitative analyses and qualitative process evaluations will be synthesized across sites to identify mechanisms of change, contextual enablers, barriers, and transferable lessons. Dissemination should include reports to participating nursing homes, practical implementation guidance for care teams, presentations to ProCon partners and long-term care stakeholders, including at international conferences, academic publications in peer-reviewed journals, and integration of findings into future versions of the ProCon continence courses.
conditions: Incontinence, Overactive Bladder, Stress Urinary Incontinence
interventions: A quasi-experimental comparative study of the effect of an educational, pragmatic intervention to improve the quality of continence care in continuing care homes
primary_outcomes: Number of fecal incontinence episodes
Continence status
Number of urinary incontinence episodes
Satisfaction with continence care
title: A Study of the Effect of an Educational Intervention to Improve Continence Care in Continuing Care Homes

brief_summary:
This study evaluated two non-drug techniques that may help women manage pain during labor: rhythmic fabric sifting (also known as Rebozo) and Shiatsu massage. The study also examined whether these techniques were associated with women's experiences of childbirth and early mother-infant bonding.

Labor pain is a common and important concern for women during childbirth. Although medications can provide pain relief, some women may prefer or benefit from non-drug approaches that can be provided as part of supportive maternity care. Rhythmic fabric sifting and Shiatsu massage are non-pharmacological techniques that may provide physical comfort and support during labor.

The study included 120 primiparous women, meaning women giving birth for the first time, who were at term pregnancy. The women were divided into three groups, with 40 women in each group. One group received routine maternity care, one group received rhythmic fabric sifting in addition to routine care, and one group received Shiatsu massage in addition to routine care.

Rhythmic fabric sifting was provided during the first stage of labor using a fabric-based technique. The technique was adjusted according to the stage of cervical dilation and was applied during contractions. Shiatsu massage was provided during different stages of the first stage of labor using specified pressure techniques at selected body points. Both interventions were provided in addition to routine maternity care.

Women's labor pain was assessed before the intervention and again after receiving the assigned intervention. The childbirth experience was assessed after delivery. Early mother-infant bonding was also assessed within the first 24 hours after birth.

The study found that women who received rhythmic fabric sifting reported lower labor pain and a more positive childbirth experience compared with women receiving routine care. Women who received Shiatsu massage also reported lower labor pain and a more positive childbirth experience compared with routine care. However, the study did not demonstrate that one intervention was superior to the other because pain was assessed at different time points after each intervention. Rhythmic fabric sifting was assessed 15 minutes after the intervention, whereas Shiatsu massage was assessed 30 minutes after the intervention. Therefore, differences between the two techniques cannot be interpreted as evidence that one treatment provides faster or greater pain relief.

No significant difference was found among the three groups in early mother-infant bonding during the first 24 hours after birth.

This study used a quasi-experimental, nonrandomized design and convenience sampling. Participants were recruited from two hospitals in the same geographic region. These features may limit how broadly the findings can be applied to other women, hospitals, or healthcare settings. In addition, the different timing of post-intervention pain assessments limits direct comparison between the two interventions.

Overall, the findings suggest that rhythmic fabric sifting and Shiatsu massage may be associated with reduced labor pain and a more positive childbirth experience among first-time mothers when used alongside routine maternity care. The findings do not establish that either technique is superior to the other or demonstrate their clinical safety. Further studies with larger samples, multiple healthcare centers, random assignment of participants, standardized pain-assessment time points, and longer follow-up are needed to confirm the effects of these techniques and evaluate their longer-term outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Labor Pain
Childbirth Experience
Mother-Infant Bonding
title: Rhythmic Fabric Sifting and Shiatsu Massage in Labor

brief_summary:
Chronic lumbar facet syndrome is an important cause of persistent low back pain and functional limitation. Lumbar medial branch radiofrequency neurotomy (RFN) is a minimally invasive treatment used in patients with facet-mediated pain confirmed by diagnostic medial branch blocks. However, because the medial branch nerves also provide motor innervation to the multifidus muscle, the potential long-term effects of RFN on paraspinal muscle volume remain uncertain.

This prospective, randomized controlled trial aims to investigate changes in multifidus and erector spinae muscle volume following conventional lumbar medial branch RFN and to evaluate whether a home-based core stabilization exercise program influences these changes.

A total of 26 patients with chronic lumbar facet syndrome will be enrolled following a positive response, defined as at least a 50% reduction in pain intensity, to fluoroscopy-guided diagnostic lumbar medial branch block. All participants will undergo conventional lumbar medial branch RFN under fluoroscopic guidance. Following RFN, participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either an RFN plus exercise group or an RFN-only group. The exercise group will receive a six-week home-based core stabilization exercise program, with adherence monitored through weekly telephone calls.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) will be used to assess multifidus and erector spinae muscle volumes before RFN and at 12 months after treatment. MRI images will be analyzed using deep learning-based automatic segmentation and computer-assisted three-dimensional volumetric analysis, with muscle volumes calculated using voxel-based methods.

Pain intensity, lumbar range of motion, functional disability, health-related quality of life, neurological examination findings, and analgesic use will be assessed at baseline and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after RFN. The study will evaluate changes in paraspinal muscle volume following RFN and the potential contribution of core stabilization exercises to muscle volume preservation and clinical outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Paraspinal Muscle Volume
Pain Intensity (Visual Analog Scale, VAS)
title: "Three-Dimensional MRI Analysis of Paraspinal Muscle Volume Following Radiofrequency Neurotomy in Chronic Lumbar Facet Syndrome: The Modulating Role of Exercise"

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the clinical and economic effectiveness of influenza vaccination among adults aged 60 years and older in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It will compare influenza-related health outcomes and healthcare costs between older adults who receive influenza vaccination and those who do not.

This is a prospective observational cohort study with a control group. The study plans to enroll 2,298 participants, including 766 vaccinated and 1,532 unvaccinated older adults. Participants will be recruited at Thong Nhat Hospital and University Medical Center Ho Chi Minh City. Vaccination status will be determined by participants' vaccination history and decisions made independently of the study.

Participants will be followed for 12 months, with follow-up assessments every three months. The study will collect information on influenza, influenza-like illness, cardiovascular events, respiratory events, hospitalization, mortality, and direct medical costs related to influenza.

The study will compare the occurrence of clinical outcomes and direct medical costs between the two groups. It will also evaluate economic measures related to influenza vaccination, including avoided treatment costs, cost savings, and the benefit-cost ratio. The findings will be used to provide scientific evidence for developing influenza vaccination policy recommendations for older adults in Ho Chi Minh City.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Confirmed Influenza
Incidence of Influenza-like Illness
Avoided Treatment Costs
Net Cost Savings
Benefit-Cost Ratio
title: Clinical and Economic Effectiveness of Influenza Vaccination in Older Adults

brief_summary: This pilot clinical trial aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of an integrated fabric-type orthosis with muscle-mimicking and proprioception-enhancing functions in older adults with geriatric conditions affecting gait and balance. The wearable orthosis provides lower-limb assistance through a fabric-based actuation system and vibrotactile proprioceptive stimulation. Thirty participants aged 65 years or older will undergo gait, balance, proprioception, and electromyography assessments under three conditions: without the orthosis, with the orthosis powered off, and with the orthosis powered on. Outcome measures include gait performance, postural sway, one-leg standing balance, joint position sense, muscle activation, physiological responses, fatigue, and device-related adverse events. The study is designed as an exploratory pilot trial to assess the clinical applicability, usability, and safety of the wearable assistive device in geriatric patients.
primary_outcomes: Change in Blood Pressure From Before to After Functional Assessment
Change in Heart Rate From Before to After Functional Assessment
Change in Perceived Exertion From Before to After Functional Assessment
Change in Pain Intensity From Before to After Functional Assessment
title: Safety and Feasibility of an Integrated Fabric-Type Orthosis for Gait and Balance Improvement in Geriatric Patients

brief_summary:
This study will compare two doses of a clot-dissolving medicine called tenecteplase (TNK), specifically recombinant human TNK tissue-type plasminogen activator for injection (rhTNK-tPA), in adults with a mild ischemic stroke that causes disabling symptoms. An ischemic stroke occurs when a blood clot blocks blood flow to the brain. Even a mild stroke can cause problems that prevent a person from carrying out basic daily activities or returning to work.

The main question is whether a lower dose of rhTNK-tPA helps patients recover nearly as well as the standard dose, within a predefined acceptable difference. The study will also compare bleeding and other side effects between the two doses.

Up to 1,324 participants at multiple hospitals will be randomly assigned to receive either the lower dose (0.18 mg/kg, up to 16 mg) or the standard dose (0.25 mg/kg, up to 25 mg). Each participant will receive one injection into a vein within 4.5 hours of stroke onset, along with usual stroke care. Participants and treating doctors will know which dose is given, but the assessors evaluating recovery will not.

Participants will be followed for approximately 90 days. Researchers will assess recovery, ability to carry out daily activities, quality of life, bleeding, and other medical problems. The main outcome is the proportion of participants who have no symptoms or no significant disability at about 90 days after treatment.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With a Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) Score of 0-1
title: Low-Dose Versus Standard-Dose Tenecteplase for Acute Minor Ischemic Stroke With Disabling Deficits

brief_summary: This prospective randomized study compares two methods of remimazolam induction in adults aged 20 to 70 years scheduled for elective single-port robotic cholecystectomy: a single intravenous bolus of 0.2 mg/kg versus continuous intravenous infusion at 12 mg/kg/hour. The primary outcome is emergence time, from discontinuation of sevoflurane to recovery of consciousness defined as a Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (MOAA/S) score of 5. Ninety participants were enrolled.
primary_outcomes: Emergence time
title: Remimazolam Induction Methods in Robotic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary:
Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) are among the most clinically relevant pancreatic cystic lesions because of their potential for malignant transformation into high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma. Accurate preoperative risk stratification is essential to identify patients who may benefit from surgical resection while avoiding unnecessary surgery in those with low-grade disease.

Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) plays a central role in the evaluation of IPMNs because it allows detailed assessment of ductal and cystic features associated with malignancy, including mural nodules, main pancreatic duct abnormalities, wall thickening, contrast enhancement, and elastography patterns. However, the combined predictive value of these features has not been fully standardized.

The IMAGE study is a single-center retrospective study designed to develop and validate a machine learning-based model integrating comprehensive EUS features to predict the presence of high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma in patients with surgically resected IPMNs. The study includes adult patients who underwent preoperative EUS at a tertiary referral center and had a final histological diagnosis of IPMN after surgery.

The primary objective is to assess the diagnostic performance of the IMAGE model for predicting high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma. Secondary objectives include evaluation of the diagnostic contribution of individual EUS feature domains and assessment of agreement between preoperative EUS classification and final histological diagnosis.
primary_outcomes: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC) of the IMAGE Model for Predicting High-Grade Dysplasia or Invasive Carcinoma
Sensitivity of the IMAGE Model for Predicting High-Grade Dysplasia or Invasive Carcinoma
Specificity of the IMAGE Model for Predicting High-Grade Dysplasia or Invasive Carcinoma
title: Endoscopic Ultrasound Predictors of Malignancy in IPMNs: Toward Personalized, Data-driven Risk Stratification

brief_summary: To compare the 12-month "treatment success" rate between a single SBRT dose of 30 Gy/1 and three SBRT doses totaling 54 Gy/3 in elderly or frail patients with early-stage NSCLC.
primary_outcomes: Overall Survival
Local Failure Free Survival
title: Comparing Single-session Versus Fractionated Stereotactic Radiotherapy for Elderly and Frail Patients With Early-stage Non-small Cell Lung Cancer.

brief_summary:
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fully decentralized (remote) clinical trial evaluating the effects of Broc Shot Capsules on skin appearance and comfort in adults with reactive, blemish-prone, or hormonally affected skin. Fifty participants aged 18-65 years will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either Broc Shot Capsules (active) or matched placebo capsules for 8 weeks.

Participants will take 2 capsules once daily and complete self-reported questionnaires and standardized self-captured skin photographs at Baseline, Week 4, and Week 8 via a secure online study platform. Expert dermatologist grading of photographs will be conducted remotely at each timepoint. The study is designed to substantiate consumer product claims related to visible skin improvement and participant-reported skin comfort, and is not intended to evaluate treatment of any clinical dermatological disease.
primary_outcomes: Clinician-Assessed Change in Overall Skin Appearance
title: A Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Effects of Broc Shot Capsules on Skin Appearance and Comfort in Adults With Reactive, Blemish-Prone, or Hormonally Affected Skin

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a daily dietary supplement called iNAD CONTROL can improve the function of the retinal ganglion cells (the nerve cells of the retina that carry visual information to the brain) in adults with open-angle glaucoma who are already being treated with eye-pressure-lowering therapy. iNAD CONTROL contains nicotinamide riboside (a form of vitamin B3), acetyl-L-carnitine, forskolin and hesperidin, which may support the energy metabolism of these nerve cells and protect them from damage.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Does taking iNAD CONTROL for 12 weeks improve retinal ganglion cell function, measured with an electroretinogram (ERG, a test that records the electrical response of the retina to light), compared with a placebo (a look-alike tablet with no active ingredients)?

Researchers will also look at whether iNAD CONTROL changes the visual field, the thickness of the retinal nerve fiber layers measured with optical coherence tomography (OCT), visual acuity and eye pressure.

Researchers will compare iNAD CONTROL with placebo. Each participant will receive both: iNAD CONTROL for 12 weeks and placebo for 12 weeks, in a random order. Neither the participants nor the study doctors will know which product is being taken in each period.

Participants will:

* Take 1 tablet a day for 24 weeks in total (12 weeks of iNAD CONTROL and 12 weeks of placebo)
* Continue their usual glaucoma eye drops without changes
* Attend 5 clinic visits over 6 months (at the start and at weeks 6, 12, 18 and 24)
* At each visit, undergo non-invasive eye tests: visual acuity, eye pressure, visual field tests, ERG and OCT, plus blood pressure and body weight measurement
primary_outcomes: Change in PhNR Peak-to-Trough Amplitude (PhNRPT)
title: Effect of a Nicotinamide Riboside-Based Dietary Supplement on Retinal Function in Glaucoma (BRIGHT)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to explore how almond food structure influences gastric emptying rates when consumed by healthy adult women as part of a standardized breakfast meal. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the structure of almonds (whole, chopped, buttered) influence gastric emptying ?
* What is the correlation between chewing behaviour, gastric emptying, and changes in postprandial triacylglycerols and satiety (hormones and ratings) within the context of an increasingly disrupted nut matrix.
conditions: This Study Explores the Relationships Between Almond Particle Size, Chewing, Gastric Emptying, and Postprandial Metabolism
primary_outcomes: Gastric emptying half-time
title: The Almond Yogurt Study (AYS)

brief_summary:
The objective of this observational study (a single-center, prospective, consecutively enrolled clinical cohort) is to establish a cohort of adult liver transplant recipients to correlate, within the same population, the recipients' preoperative status with graft condition, perioperative medical and therapeutic exposures, and dynamic physiological changes, as well as multiorgan outcomes and functional recovery; to identify factors associated with organ injury and difficulties in recovery; and to provide a basis for subsequent clinical validation and intervention studies. The study population consists of adult recipients aged ≥18 years who are scheduled to undergo their first single-liver transplant at this center; continuous enrollment is planned for 5 years, with a target of 450 participants, each followed for 12 months. Recipients undergoing repeat liver transplantation or combined organ transplantation will be included only in a separate expanded registry and analysis.

The primary research questions it aims to address are:

What is the incidence rate and 95% confidence interval of the patient-level composite outcome-defined as all-cause mortality or at least one of the predefined major organ complications (early graft dysfunction/graft failure, new-onset or worsening moderate-to-severe acute kidney injury, new-onset delirium or confirmed acute neurological event, major cardiovascular event, or major pulmonary complication)-within 30 days after the start of the transplant procedure? After accounting for preoperative disease severity, organ function, and graft condition, how are perioperative clinical exposures and physiological changes-such as circulatory, respiratory, temperature, and EEG parameters-associated with multiorgan outcomes and functional recovery at 12 months? Can prespecified dynamic physiological data provide additional information regarding risk or recovery beyond routine clinical data?

This study has no control group; no treatment will be assigned; routine monitoring, testing, or rehabilitation arrangements will not be altered; and no additional blood draws or tissue samples will be collected. Participants will:

Undergo preoperative baseline data collection and assessments of cognition, frailty, functional status, and quality of recovery; some participants will complete the sleep and mood extension modules (PSQI, HADS).

During the perioperative period, participants will allow the research team to record clinically generated treatment exposures and multimodal monitoring data, including circulatory, respiratory, temperature, and EEG parameters.

Participants will complete relevant follow-up visits and functional assessments on postoperative days 7, 30, and 90, as well as at 6 and 12 months, including the QoR-15, DAH-30/90, and assessments of cognition, frailty, functional status, and quality of life.

Follow-up should preferably be conducted in conjunction with routine follow-up visits; when necessary, survival, hospitalization, and living conditions may be verified via approved telephone contact. Additional clinical testing using residual serum and tissue samples is optional; refusal to provide these samples will not affect enrollment in the study.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with all-cause mortality or at least one major organ complication within 30 days after the start of transplant surgery, assessed according to preset clinical criteria (e.g., Olthoff definition, KDIGO criteria).
title: A Single-Center, Prospective Clinical Cohort Study on Perioperative Management, Exposure, Multiorgan Outcomes, and Functional Recovery in Liver Transplantation

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to examine how people with plantar fasciitis differ from matched healthy controls in terms of ankle dorsiflexor/plantar flexor ratio (measured by Isokinetic dynamometry, IKD), pain intensity (measured by visual analogue scale, VAS), dynamic balance (assessed by Y-balance test), functional performance (assessed by foot function index, FFI), and ankle range of motion (measured by the goniometer).

Ankle dorsiflexor peak torque at 120°/s
Ankle plantar-flexor peak torque at 30°/s
Ankle plantar-flexor peak torque at 120°/s
Ankle dorsiflexor-to-plantar-flexor peak torque ratio at 30°/s
Ankle dorsiflexor-to-plantar-flexor peak torque ratio at 120°/s
title: Isokinetic Evaluation of Ankle Dorsiflexor to Planter Flexor Strength Ratio in Patients With Plantar Fasciitis

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study evaluates the effects of an artificial intelligence-assisted diabetes education video on quality of life, diabetes self-management skills, and glycemic control in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus. Participants are assigned to an intervention group receiving a 12-minute educational video through a Meta Quest 2 virtual reality headset or a control group receiving routine diabetes education and care. Outcomes are assessed at baseline and at three months using validated questionnaires and routinely recorded HbA1c values.
primary_outcomes: Diabetes-Specific Quality of Life
Diabetes Self-Management Skills
Glycemic Control (HbA1c)
title: AI-Assisted Diabetes Education for Children With Type 1 Diabetes

brief_summary:
Background:

Dyslipidemia (raised blood cholesterol) is a widespread public health concern in Hong Kong. While medications like statins are commonly used, many individuals hesitate to take them, making effective dietary strategies essential for reducing cardiovascular disease risk. The Portfolio Diet is a proven plant-based dietary pattern that can significantly lower cholesterol levels, but its feasibility has not yet been thoroughly explored or culturally adapted for a non-Western population like Hong Kong.

Purpose:

This feasibility study aims to evaluate whether a culturally tailored Portfolio Diet health education programme is practical, acceptable, and effective for Hong Kong adults with dyslipidemia. The findings will help researchers understand the practical challenges and motivators participants face when trying to change their diet, which will guide the design of a future larger-scale trial.

Methods:

A total of 12 Chinese adults aged 18 to 65 with borderline or high total cholesterol will participate in a 4-week health education programme. The programme begins with a group session explaining the core dietary principles, followed by 3 weekly individual dietary consultations with a research dietitian. The diet plan and sample 7-day menus are culturally adapted to include food items commonly consumed in Chinese culture.

Participants' diet adherence will be assessed using 3-day dietary records at the beginning and end of the study. Additionally, researchers will track feasibility data such as recruitment and retention rates, session attendance, and the completeness of the dietary records. Following the 4-week programme, participants will join focus group interviews to share their personal feedback, experiences, and suggestions for improving the programme for long-term use.
interventions: Culturally Adapted Portfolio Diet Health Education Programme
primary_outcomes: Programme Retention Rate
Change in Portfolio Diet Adherence Score
title: Portfolio Diet for Dyslipidemia: A Hong Kong Pilot Study

brief_summary: This prospective multicenter observational study enrolls children aged 2-17 years receiving preoperative anxiolysis and separation support prior to general anesthesia. Subjects receive intranasal dexmedetomidine spray (1-2.5 μg/kg). Key assessments include Ramsay sedation score within 45 min post-drug, intraoperative MSS aspiration risk score, postoperative agitation, mYPAS/GAD-7 anxiety, PedSQoR recovery and behavioral scores, plus ongoing adverse event documentation (respiratory depression, bradycardia, etc.). The primary aim is to assess real-world efficacy and safety of intranasal dexmedetomidine across pediatric age groups and optimize medication strategies for pediatric comfortable anesthesia. Safety follow-up lasts from consent signing until 7 days after Visit 8.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants achieving Ramsay Sedation Score ≥3 at least once within 45 minutes after drug administration
title: A Prospective, Multicenter, Observational Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Dexmedetomidine Hydrochloride Nasal Spray for Preoperative Sedation in Children Under General Anesthesia

brief_summary:
More than 300 million surgical procedures are performed worldwide each year. However, surgical errors remain among the most common medical errors causing preventable patient harm. Although various health policies have been implemented globally and nationally, adverse events continue to occur due to factors such as high patient volumes and insufficient staffing. One of the most important initiatives developed to prevent surgery-related adverse events is the World Health Organization's "Safe Surgery Saves Lives" project. Within this initiative, the Surgical Safety Checklist was developed and has contributed to significant reductions in adverse events. The World Health Organization has encouraged countries to adapt the checklist to their healthcare systems. In Türkiye, it was revised by adding an additional section based on the principle that "Safe surgery starts in the clinic."

Current patient safety policies and initiatives largely focus on healthcare professionals. However, developing a culture of surgical safety should begin during undergraduate education. After graduation, students may adopt existing institutional practices regarding patient and surgical safety. Therefore, developing nursing students' knowledge, skills, and professional judgment regarding safe surgery before graduation is essential.

This randomized controlled experimental study aims to compare the effectiveness of an artificial intelligence-assisted virtual simulation game and traditional simulation in improving nursing students' knowledge and skills regarding the Surgical Safety Checklist. The effects of these interventions on students' problem-solving skills and patient safety competencies will also be examined. Students, research fellows, and the statistician will be blinded. Data will be collected using the Surgical Safety Checklist Knowledge Test, Surgical Safety Checklist Skills Assessment Checklist, Problem Solving Inventory, and a scale assessing nursing students' patient safety competencies. Data will be analyzed using SPSS, with p\<0.05 considered statistically significant.
primary_outcomes: Nursing Students' Surgical Safety Checklist Knowledge Test Score
Nursing Students' Surgical Safety Checklist Skills Assessment Checklist Score
title: AI-Assisted vs. Traditional Simulation for Safe Surgery Checklist Knowledge and Skills

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out whether adding intercostal nerve cryoablation to intercostal nerve blocks with levobupivacaine improves pain relief after minimally invasive surgery for lung cancer. Both treatments target nerves between the ribs. Levobupivacaine is a local anesthetic that temporarily blocks pain signals. Cryoablation uses very low temperatures to temporarily interrupt nerve function and may provide longer-lasting pain relief.

The study will include 80 adults undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) to remove a lung lobe or a smaller anatomical part of the lung at University Medical Centre Maribor, Slovenia.

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups, with 40 participants in each group:

* The cryoablation group will receive intercostal nerve cryoablation at three levels together with intercostal nerve blocks with levobupivacaine at five levels.
* The comparison group will receive intercostal nerve blocks with levobupivacaine at five levels without cryoablation.

Both groups will receive the same standard approach to pain medicines after surgery, with additional pain relief as needed.

The main question is whether adding cryoablation reduces pain during the first 72 hours after surgery. Participants will rate their pain at rest and when coughing at 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours after surgery.

Researchers will also compare opioid pain medicine use, the need for additional pain relief, recovery after surgery, and side effects or complications. Follow-up assessments at 1, 3, and 6 months will evaluate persistent pain and changes in sensation, including numbness, tingling, or burning pain.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative pain intensity at rest and during coughing measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)
title: Cryoablation Versus Standard Nerve Block for Pain Control After Lung Surgery

brief_summary: This study addresses an unmet need to improve the diagnostic accuracy of: 1. supplemental breast cancer screening with whole breast US and 2. the evaluation of disease extent in women with newly diagnosed breast cancer.
interventions: QT Scanner: Quantitative Transmission Ultrasound Breast Imaging System

brief_summary:
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause is a common condition that can affect women after the menopause. It may cause vaginal dryness, soreness, pain during sex, urinary symptoms and a reduced quality of life. Standard treatments include vaginal moisturisers, lubricants and vaginal oestrogen. Some women do not respond fully to these treatments, cannot use oestrogen, or prefer an alternative option.

This study will look at outcomes following treatment with MonaLisa Touch, a fractional carbon dioxide laser treatment. "Fractional carbon dioxide laser" means that a medical laser is used to deliver small, controlled areas of heat to the vaginal tissue. The aim is to stimulate healing and improve symptoms. This study will not test a new treatment or change the patient's usual care. It will observe patients who are already receiving MonaLisa Touch treatment as part of routine clinical practice.

The main question is whether patients report improvement in their symptoms and quality of life after treatment, and whether any side effects or complications occur. The study will also help doctors and patients better understand longer-term outcomes following treatment.

Participants will be women with symptoms of genitourinary syndrome of menopause who are being considered for, or are receiving, MonaLisa Touch treatment. Participation will involve giving consent for information about their symptoms, treatment and follow-up to be collected and analysed. This may include questionnaires before and after treatment. Taking part is voluntary and will not affect the care offered.

The study will be conducted in a private clinical setting at Clarendon Health. It is expected to run as an ongoing observational study, with participants followed up after treatment as part of routine care.

The research is funded by Clarendon Health and no personal identifying information will be included in published results.
interventions: Co2 fractitional ablative vaginal laser therapy
primary_outcomes: Change in overall GSM symptom severity using a predefined composite 0-10 score
title: Mona Lisa Touch Clinical Outcomes Registry

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to evaluate role of perioperative Dexmedetomidine on intraoperative hemodynamics and neuro-endocrine response in patients undergoing Robot-Assisted gynecological surgery.
conditions: Perioperative Role of Dexmedetomidine on Cortisol Level in Robotic Hysterectomy
primary_outcomes: Serum Cortisol Level
title: Role of Perioperative Dexmedetomidine on Intraoperative Hemodynamics and Neuro-endocrine Response in Patients Undergoing Robot-Assisted Gynecological Surgery

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate the effect of Elongation Longitudinal Décoaptation Ostéo-Articulaire versus Global Postural Re-education Exercises on Cervical Radiculopathy. The main question it aims to answer is: Is there a difference between the effect of ELDOA and GPR on Pain , Cervical Range of Motion , Neck Functional Disability, and Proprioception in CR patients?
conditions: Cervical Radiculopathy at C6 Nerve Root
primary_outcomes: pain intensity assessment
Neck Functional Disability Level
title: ELDOA Versus GPR Exercises in Cervical Radiculopathy

brief_summary: CUG279-P101 is a first-in-human, open-label, multicenter Phase 1 study evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, immune-pharmacodynamics, and preliminary antitumor activity of CUG279 in adults with select unresectable advanced or metastatic solid tumors.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of dose limiting toxicities (DLTs)
Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)

Clinically significant changes in safety laboratory parameters from baseline
