Incidence of TEAEs leading to dose modifications
title: A Phase I Dose-Escalation Study of CUG279 in Participants With Select Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if adding automated robotic Tuina to acupuncture yields a better outcome than acupuncture alone in treating adults with chronic nonspecific low back pain. It will also learn about the safety of the automated robotic Tuina. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does robotic Tuina and acupuncture reduces score of Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) more than acupuncture alone? Does it improve the sleep, quality of life, pain related impact of participants? Researchers will compare automated robotic Tuina and acupuncture to acupuncture alone if the combination works better to treat chronic nonspecific low back pain.

Participants will:

Receive weekly treatment of either automated robotic Tuina and acupuncture or acupuncture only for 6 sessions over 8 weeks.

Visit the clinic weekly for interventions and test. Wear a sleep tracker ring on the night before and night of treatment to sleep.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in pain intensity. Visual analogue scale.
title: Efficacy of Automated Tuina and Acupuncture for Treating Chronic Lower Back Pain

brief_summary:
This study examined whether a 12-week after-school Latin dance program could improve mental health in primary school children aged 9 to 12 who were identified through school screening as being at risk of mental health difficulties.

Forty-eight children were assigned by chance to one of two groups, with 24 children in each group. One group took part in after-school cha-cha and rumba sessions three times a week. The other group continued its usual physical activities.

Children in both groups completed questionnaires before the program began and shortly after it ended. The researchers expected that children in the dance group would have greater reductions in anxiety and emotional and behavioral difficulties, and greater improvements in overall well-being.
conditions: Mental Health in Elementary School Children
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) Score
Change from Baseline in Mental Health Rating Scale for Primary School Students (MHRSP) Total Score
Change from Baseline in General Well-Being Schedule (GWB) Total Score
title: Latin Dance and Mental Health in Primary School Children

brief_summary: This study is being done to learn whether people with neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) that have spread to the liver can safely tolerate a lower dose of everolimus after bland hepatic artery embolization (HAE).
primary_outcomes: Percentage of patients who can tolerate everolimus pre and post HAE
title: Everolimus Post-Bland Hepatic Artery Embolization in Patients With Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs) With Liver Metastasis

brief_summary: High quality early intervention offers significant benefits for autistic children, yet most programs fail to adjust the level of support needed to sustain parent engagement and maximize efficacy. We will utilize a Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trial (SMART) trial, an implementation research design in which participants are re-randomized at key decision points, to explore methods to improve engagement in OPT-In-Early (Online Parent Training in Early Behavioral Intervention). OPT-In-Early is a self-directed online autism parent-training program that teaches evidence-based behavioral/developmental strategies to promote child skill development and reduce interfering behaviors. In this adaptive intervention, parents will first be randomized to either OPT-In-Early or OPT-In-Early with automated support. We will monitor progress and intervene early (during Month 1 of the 6-month intervention) to identify parents who either (1) demonstrate low engagement with the program or (2) use the program but do not learn information. These parents needing extra support will then be re-randomized to receive additional remote clinical support, either in the form of group or individual intervention. The intervention will be based on OPT-In-Early principles. An adaptive approach to OPT-In-Early may improve child outcomes while using resources more judiciously.
interventions: Online Parent Training in Early Behavioral Intervention (OPT-In-Early)
primary_outcomes: Autism Impact Measure
MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories
title: An Adaptive Parent-mediated Intervention to Improve Outcomes for Autistic Children

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational prospective cohort study is to explore the impacts and potential molecular mechanisms of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease/non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NAFLD/NASH) on extrahepatic organ injury in adult patients scheduled for partial hepatectomy. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do patients with NAFLD/NASH suffer more severe extrahepatic organ injury compared with patients without NAFLD/NASH? Are inflammatory mediators (IL-2, IL-6, IL-11) associated with the severity of NAFLD/NASH and extrahepatic organ damage?

Researchers will compare the NAFLD/NASH group (n=18) with the non-NAFLD/NASH group (n=18) to see if NAFLD/NASH aggravates extrahepatic organ injury and correlates with elevated levels of serum and urinary inflammatory mediators .

Participants will:

* Provide 3 mL preoperative venous blood sample and 5 mL mid-stream urine sample for detection of inflammatory mediators.
* Undergo partial hepatectomy; small pieces of resected liver tissue will be collected for HE staining and Oil-Red-O staining for histopathological evaluation and disease-staging.
* Complete routine preoperative baseline assessments including demographic data, medical history, laboratory tests and instrumental examinations.
* Receive clinical laboratory and instrumental examinations related to liver and extrahepatic organ function within 7 days after surgery for outcome evaluation.
primary_outcomes: Differences in laboratory and instrumental examination results related to various extrahepatic organs related to various extrahepatic organs between the two groups
title: Prospective Cohort Study of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease and Non-alcoholic Steatohepatitis Aggravating Extrahepatic Organ Damage

brief_summary: The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to learn whether a virtual reality-supported child abuse and body safety education program improves fourth-year nursing students' awareness of child abuse and neglect, their ability to recognize its signs and risk factors, and their attitudes toward reporting it. The main questions it aims to answer are: - Do students who receive the program score higher in recognizing the signs and risks of child abuse and neglect than students who do not? - Do they have higher awareness of child abuse and neglect and more positive attitudes toward reporting child abuse? - Are these effects still present one month after the program ends? Researchers will compare an intervention group, which takes part in an 8-week face-to-face program (one 90-minute session per week) ending with a virtual reality simulation, with a control group that receives no training during the study. Control group students will be offered the same training after the study ends. Participants will: - Complete questionnaires before the program, after the program, and one month later - If assigned to the intervention group, attend weekly education sessions and take part in a short virtual reality simulation in week 8
interventions: VR-Supported Child Abuse and Body Safety Education
primary_outcomes: Recognition of Signs and Risks of Child Abuse and Neglect
title: Virtual Reality-Supported Child Abuse and Body Safety Education for Nursing Students

brief_summary: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) is an aggressive type of lung cancer. Current treatment options are limited, and response to treatment may not last long. Outcomes are especially poor when the cancer has spread to the brain. This study tests whether a new treatment: risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez) with atezolizumab works better than standard of care treatment. Ris-Rez is designed to deliver cancer-killing medicine directly to cancer cells. Atezolizumab helps the immune system attack cancer cells. Researchers will see if this combination helps people live longer and keeps the cancer from getting worse.
primary_outcomes: Overall survival (OS)
Progression-free survival (PFS) by Blinded independent central review (BICR) assessment
title: A Study of Risvutatug Rezetecan in Combination With Atezolizumab in Participants With Extensive Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer (EMBOLD-SCLC-303)

brief_summary: Catheter-related bladder discomfort (CRBD) is common after holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP). This single-center, randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded trial evaluates whether an ultrasound-guided bilateral sacral erector spinae plane (S-ESP) block performed before general anesthesia reduces the incidence of CRBD compared with general anesthesia alone in men aged 50 to 80 years undergoing elective HoLEP. The primary outcome is the incidence of CRBD at 1 hour after surgery.
interventions: Ultrasound-guided bilateral sacral erector spinae plane block
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Catheter-Related Bladder Discomfort (CRBD) at Postoperative 1 Hour
title: Sacral Erector Spinae Plane Block for Catheter-Related Bladder Discomfort After HoLEP

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect of an imagery- and breath-based sound intervention on rumination, stress, and sleep quality among health sciences students. Participants will be randomly assigned to either an intervention group receiving a daily guided imagery and breath-based sound program or a control group receiving no intervention. Outcomes will be assessed using validated self-report questionnaires before and after the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Ruminative Thinking Style Scale (Appendix-2)
title: Imagery- and Breath-Based Sound Intervention in Health Sciences Students

brief_summary:
This study evaluates the effects of the Etta Vita GLP-1 supplement on appetite, gut health, and blood sugar over a 12-week period. Thirty participants with a BMI of 25 or greater and experiencing at least two of the following issues - food cravings, poor appetite control, irregular bowel movements, bloating, or gut issues - will use the test product daily.

The trial is a single-arm, open-label study in which all participants take two capsules of the supplement each morning, no more than 15 minutes before their first meal. Participants complete questionnaires at Baseline, Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12, and attend their local clinic for blood tests (HbA1c, Glucose, and Leptin) at Baseline and Week 12.
primary_outcomes: Change in Blood Glucose via blood test
Change in HbA1c via blood test
Change in Leptin via blood test
Change in Appetite via self-reported questionnaire
title: A Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Effects of a Supplement on Appetite, Gut Health, and Blood Sugar

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether the level of fear of childbirth before active labor is related to how the baby is born, how intense labor pain is, and whether epidural pain relief is requested, in first-time mothers with a full-term pregnancy who plan a vaginal birth.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do women with severe fear of childbirth have a higher rate of unplanned (emergency) cesarean delivery?
* Do women with more fear of childbirth feel more intense labor pain?
* Do women with more fear of childbirth ask for an epidural more often, and earlier in labor?

Researchers will compare women with severe fear of childbirth (a score of 85 or higher on the Wijma Delivery Expectancy/Experience Questionnaire, version A, or W-DEQ-A) with women whose scores are below 85.

Participants will:

* Fill out the Turkish version of the W-DEQ-A, a 33-item questionnaire about thoughts and feelings regarding the coming birth. It is completed once after admission to the labor ward, before active labor and before any pain relief, and takes about 10 to 15 minutes.
* Rate their labor pain on a scale from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst imaginable pain) during active labor and, if they ask for an epidural, at the time of the request.
* Receive routine labor care. The study does not change any treatment or clinical decision; information on labor, pain relief and delivery will be collected from hospital records.

The study will take place at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital in Ankara, Türkiye.
interventions: Wijma Delivery Expectancy/Experience Questionnaire, Version A (W-DEQ-A)
primary_outcomes: Rate of Intrapartum (Unplanned) Cesarean Delivery
title: Fear of Childbirth and Its Association With Mode of Delivery, Labor Pain, and Epidural Analgesia Request in First-Time Mothers

brief_summary:
Kidney stones are a common condition that can recur even after successful treatment. Regular imaging tests can help detect new stones, but frequent use of X-rays and CT scans can expose patients to unnecessary radiation. It is not yet clear how often patients should have imaging tests after treatment.

This study compares two schedules for monitoring patients who have undergone treatment for kidney stones and have no significant remaining stones. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group has an ultrasound examination of the kidneys and urinary tract every 6 months, while the other group has the same examination every 12 months.

The study aims to determine whether more frequent ultrasound examinations can reduce unexpected episodes related to kidney stones, such as pain, bleeding in the urine, or urinary infections caused by blocked urine flow.

The researchers will also assess changes in kidney function, visits to the emergency department, the number of imaging tests performed, the development or growth of stones without symptoms, and the overall cost of imaging.

The study includes adults with a low or high risk of kidney stones recurrence and is conducted at Sismanoglio General Hospital in Athens, Greece.

The findings may help determine an appropriate schedule for monitoring patients after kidney stone treatment while reducing unnecessary tests, radiation exposure, and healthcare costs.
lead_sponsor: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Symptomatic Stone Episodes
title: Imaging Follow-up After Stone Treatment

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate the prevalence and severity of periodontal diseases among university students from three different national backgrounds (Iranian, Sudanese, and Turkish) and to evaluate their response to periodontal treatment.

A total of 348 students will be included in the study, comprising 116 Iranian, 116 Sudanese, and 116 Turkish students. Periodontal health assessments will be performed, and all participants will receive periodontal treatment according to the study protocol.

The study will compare periodontal disease prevalence and severity among the three groups and evaluate changes in periodontal health following treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change in Probing Pocket Depth (PPD)
title: Periodontal Health and Treatment Outcomes in Students From Three Countries

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to determine the effect of cervico-thoracic junction manipulation combined with therapeutic exercises on dynamic balance and postural control in individuals with chronic neck pain, compared with therapeutic exercises alone.
primary_outcomes: Berg Balance Scale (BBS)
Neck Disability Index (NDI)
Forward Head Posture / Postural Alignment
Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS)
title: Effects of Cervicothoracic Junction Manipulation Among Chronic Neck Pain

brief_summary: This is a Phase I/II, single-arm, open-label, exploratory study aimed at evaluating the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) combined with gemcitabine and iparomlimab-toripalimab in patients with borderline resectable pancreatic cancer. The study is divided into two phases: The Phase Ib dose-escalation phase will use a "3+3" design to explore the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of SBRT (6 Gy×5 F, 7 Gy×5 F, 8 Gy×5 F) combined with gemcitabine and iparomlimab-toripalimab. The Phase II phase will further evaluate the efficacy and safety of this combination regimen based on the SBRT dose determined in Phase Ib. The primary efficacy endpoint is the R0 resection rate.
lead_sponsor: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate, ORR
Incidence of Adverse Events
title: A Phase I/II Single-Arm, Open-Label, Exploratory Study Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy (SBRT) Combined With Gemcitabine and Iparomlimab-Toripalimab in Borderline Resectable Pancreatic Cancer

brief_summary:
The present study is an online-based investigation involving adolescents with abdominal pain disorders, defined as recurrent abdominal pain persisting for at least two months. The study aims to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and effectiveness of online therapeutic interventions in comparison with usual pediatric gastroenterological care.

The study has two primary objectives. The first is to make two therapeutic interventions-Movement Motivation and Self-management Training (M3 Training) and gut-directed hypnotherapy-available online in Hungarian to young people with abdominal pain disorders and their families. Providing these interventions in an online format may facilitate easier and more timely access to therapeutic support for adolescents experiencing abdominal symptoms.

The second objective is to evaluate the effectiveness of the two online interventions. Specifically, the effectiveness of M3 Training and gut-directed hypnotherapy will be assessed both as individual interventions and in combination, and compared with usual pediatric gastroenterological care. This evaluation will assess whether the online interventions, delivered individually or in combination, offer effective therapeutic options for adolescents with abdominal pain disorders, focusing on both primary and secondary outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Pain intensity (proportion of patients with ≥30% improvement in abdominal pain) measured by Numerical Rating Scale
Quality of Life measured by The Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory
title: Effectiveness of Online Gut-Directed Hypnotherapy and Movement Motivational and Self-management Training for Abdominal Pain Disorders in Adolescents

brief_summary: This study comprised of 3 parts, gradually investigating the safety, tolerance, PK and PD characteristics of the ZL-65 tablets in healthy adult participants and obesity with cardiovascular risk participants in Australia. The study results will provide important basis for formulating the subsequent study strategies and dosing plans.Part 1: Single-ascending Dose (SAD) study and Food Effect (FE) study；Part 2: Multiple-ascending Doses (MAD) study；Part 3: Obesity with cardiovascular risk study.
interventions: Single-ascending Dose (SAD) study and Food Effect (FE) study
lead_sponsor: Chengdu Zenitar Biomedical Technology Co., Ltd

title: A Phase I Clinical Study of Oral ZL-65 Tablets in Healthy and Obese Participants With Cardiovascular Risk

brief_summary:
This prospective observational study aims to develop and evaluate prediction models for low blood oxygen levels (hypoxemia) in adult patients undergoing gastroscopy, colonoscopy, or combined gastrointestinal endoscopy under anesthesia. The study will also assess patient flow and waiting times during different stages of endoscopy care.

Low blood oxygen levels may occur during anesthesia and recovery from endoscopy. Medical-grade wireless wearable monitoring devices can continuously record vital signs as patients move through preparation, examination, transfer, and recovery areas. The investigators will analyze monitoring data, routine clinical information, and the time spent at different stages of care to identify factors associated with hypoxemia and potentially avoidable nonmedical waiting time.

This study will be conducted at the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University. Approximately 772 adult participants are planned for enrollment in the current study phase. All participants will receive routine anesthesia, endoscopy, monitoring, and recovery care. The study will not change clinical treatment decisions, and prediction model results will not be used to guide patient care.

The findings may support future improvements in patient safety monitoring, hypoxemia risk assessment, and endoscopy workflow efficiency. Participants may not receive any direct medical benefit from taking part in this study.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Hypoxemia During Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
Cumulative System-Attributable Nonmedical Waiting Time
title: An Observational Study of the Medical-Grade Wireless Wearable Data for Predicting Hypoxemia Risk and Evaluating Workflow Efficiency in Patients Undergoing Sedated Gastrointestinal Endoscopy

brief_summary: This study will examine whether sotagliflozin, a medication that may protect the heart and kidneys, can improve long-term health in people who have received a kidney transplant. The study will compare sotagliflozin with an inactive placebo in approximately 900 adult kidney transplant recipients. Researchers will assess whether the medication can reduce the risk of kidney transplant failure, worsening kidney function, heart problems, stroke, heart attack, heart failure, and death. The study will also closely monitor participants for possible side effects, including infections, dehydration, fractures, and rejection of the transplanted kidney.
primary_outcomes: Hierarchical Composite of All-Cause Mortality, Kidney Transplant Loss, Non-Fatal Stroke or Myocardial Infarction, Sustained 40% Decline in eGFR, Heart Failure Events, and Total eGFR Slope
Number of Participants Experiencing Serious Adverse Events
Number of Participants Experiencing Adverse Events Leading to Permanent Study Drug Discontinuation
Number of Participants Experiencing Study Drug-Related Adverse Events
Number of Participants Experiencing Adverse Events of Special Interest
title: Cardiovascular and Renal Protection With SGLT Inhibition in Kidney Transplant Recipients: The RENAISSANCE Trial

brief_summary:
Postbiotic metabolites produced by beneficial bacteria may influence inflammatory responses, mucosal immunity, and host physiological signalling. PosBion® contains the proprietary cell-free metabolite preparations LPM5 and LPM11, derived from Lactiplantibacillus plantarum RS5 and RI11, respectively.

This study will evaluate changes in a panel of salivary biomarkers following 12 weeks of PosBion® supplementation in adults with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). The biomarkers include myeloperoxidase (MPO), zonulin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), LPS-binding protein (LBP), cortisol, serotonin, secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA), lactoferrin, interleukin-8 (IL-8), immunoglobulin E (IgE), immunoglobulin M (IgM), and immunoglobulin G (IgG).

The study will primarily evaluate changes in inflammatory activity, while additional biomarkers will be used to explore mucosal immune, neuroendocrine, immunoglobulin, microbial exposure, and barrier-related responses following supplementation.
interventions: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum RS5- and RI11-Derived Postbiotic Metabolite Supplement
primary_outcomes: Change in Salivary Interleukin-8 (IL-8) Concentration
Change in Salivary Myeloperoxidase (MPO)
Change in Salivary Lactoferrin
Change in Salivary Secretory Immunoglobulin A (sIgA)
Change in Salivary IgE
Change in Salivary IgM
Change in Salivary IgG
title: Effects of PosBion® Supplementation on Intestinal Barrier Function in Adults With Irritable Bowel Syndrome

brief_summary: This study investigates whether acute pelvic pain with haemoperitoneum is associated with an increased risk of developing deep pelvic endometriosis, compared with acute pelvic pain without haemoperitoneum. Women aged 18-50 who attended the Obstetric-Gynecological Emergency Department for acute pelvic pain between January 2020 and December 2024 will be invited to a single follow-up visit, including a transvaginal ultrasound and validated questionnaires.

title: Development of dEep EndometrioSis Following Acute haemoPerITonEum

brief_summary: Prospective, Multi-Center, Randomized, Parallel-Controlled, Uptake clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of renal denervation in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and chronic kidney disease.

title: A Study on the Pharmacokinetics and Safety of GST-HG141 Tablets in Participants With Hepatic Impairment and Normal Liver Function

brief_summary: This is a first-in-human study of DFI205, an investigational bispecific antibody that binds CD20 and CD40, with the goal of targeting both B- and T-cell function in adults with active systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) despite standard therapy. In Phase 1, participants with RA, SLE, SSc or IIM will receive a single dose at increasing dose levels to establish safety and initial treatment response. The selected dose will be carried forward into Phase 2a, where participants will receive monthly doses to assess safety and treatment response.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the initial safety and tolerability of DFI205 in adults with SARDs
To monitor immune reconstitution after completion of dosing with DFI205
To monitor immune response to DFI205
title: Dual-targeting of B & T Cell Pathways Evaluation Trial

brief_summary:
The study was designed as a prospective, randomized, controlled trial. Patients scheduled for laparotomy will undergo anxiety level assessments and spirometry testing (baseline values) one day prior to surgery. On the morning of the operation, patients will be divided into three groups:

Group 1 (Music + Positive Suggestions): Patients will listen to therapeutic suggestions accompanied by music through headphones before surgery.

Group 2 (Music): Patients will listen only to music through headphones.

Group 3 (Control): No auditory intervention will be applied.

Following this intervention, all patients will again undergo preoperative anxiety level assessments and spirometry testing (second measurement). During general anesthesia, Groups 1 and 2 will continue to receive their respective auditory interventions via headphones, while the control group will not receive any auditory input. Hemodynamic parameters and spirometry data from the anesthesia machine will be recorded intraoperatively.

In the postoperative recovery room, Aldrete recovery scores, Apfel postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) scores, VAS pain scores, time to first analgesic requirement, total analgesic consumption within 24 hours, and postoperative spirometry values will be evaluated. At 24 hours after surgery, patients will complete a quality of recovery questionnaire and a short patient satisfaction survey.
conditions: Effects of Music and Positive Suggestions Under General Anesthesia on Respiratory Function Changes
interventions: Music Combined With Positive Verbal Suggestions
primary_outcomes: Change in Forced Expiratory Volume in One Second (FEV1) Following Intraoperative Music and Positive Suggestions
Change in Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) Following Intraoperative Music and Positive Suggestions
Change in the Ratio of Forced Expiratory Volume in One Second to Forced Vital Capacity (FEV1/FVC) Following Intraoperative Music and Positive Suggestions
Change in Peak Expiratory Flow (PEF) Following Intraoperative Music and Positive Suggestions
title: Evaluation of the Effect of Positive Suggestion During Gynecological Laparotomies on Respiratory Functions and Patient Satisfaction

brief_summary: This study evaluates the immediate effects of a single session of neuroathletic training on flexibility, balance, trunk muscle endurance, and knee position sense in adults aged 18 to 35 years. Neuroathletic training combines eye movement and head movement tasks with selected body movements. Sedentary and physically active participants receive the same training session. Physical performance is assessed before and immediately after the session. The study examines changes after training and whether these changes differ according to participants' usual physical activity levels.
primary_outcomes: Change in Sit-and-Reach Distance
title: Immediate Effects of Neuroathletic Training in Sedentary and Physically Active Adults

brief_summary: Living kidney donors undergoing laparoscopic donor nephrectomy will be randomized to receive either an erector spinae plane block (ESPB) or a combination of external oblique intercostal (EOI) and lateral external oblique muscle plane (lateral EXOP) blocks at the end of surgery. The study aims to compare postoperative pain scores, opioid consumption, rescue analgesic requirement and postoperative nausea and vomiting between the two groups.
interventions: External Oblique Intercostal Plane Block and Lateral External Oblique Muscle Plane Block combination
primary_outcomes: Pain score at 8th hour
title: Erector Spinae Plane Block Versus External Oblique Intercostal Plus Lateral External Oblique Muscle Plane Block in Laparoscopic Living Donor Nephrectomy

brief_summary: PREV-AR NICU was a national, multicenter, cross-sectional point-prevalence study conducted in 58 neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) in Argentina during April 2026. All patients present in a participating NICU during a 24-hour period were included. Active infection was classified as infection without sepsis, probable sepsis, confirmed sepsis, or septic shock. Colonization by multidrug-resistant organisms (MDRO) was assessed by rectal and nasal swabs. Patients were followed for in-NICU mortality. Mixed-effects logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of infection and mortality.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of infection among NICU patients
title: Burden of Infections and Antimicrobial Resistance in Neonatal Intensive Care Units in Argentina (PREV-AR NICU): A National Point-Prevalence Study

brief_summary:
The PREOP-RAD study aims to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of preoperative surgical resection (SRS) in patients with large brain metastases requiring surgical resection, taking into account potential differences based on sex/gender, compared to postoperative SRS, within the Spanish healthcare context.

More specifically, the study seeks to:

* Assess the clinical and radiological outcomes of the preoperative strategy in terms of local control, progression-free survival, and the occurrence of radionecrosis or neuromuscular dysfunction (nMD) compared to the postoperative strategy.
* Study the histopathological profile of resected lesions before and after SRS, searching for personalized biomarkers of response and toxicity.
* Identify patterns based on radiomic analysis and advanced imaging related to therapeutic response, recurrence, and complications.

PREOP-RAD is a prospective, randomized, multicenter study that will include patients diagnosed with symptomatic, single or multiple brain metastases ≥2 cm who are candidates for surgical resection. The procedure will consist of preoperative administration of SRS (1-5 fractions, depending on location and size), followed by surgery within a maximum of 10 days.

The intervention will be carried out in coordination with the Neurosurgery and Radiation Oncology Departments of each participating center, using a standardized workflow. The collection of surgical samples will allow for centralized histopathological studies. Furthermore, pre- and postoperative images will undergo radiomic analysis using artificial intelligence tools to explore similarities and correlate morphological and textural characteristics with clinical outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Locoregional adverse event-free survival
title: Preoperative and Postoperative Radiosurgery in Patients With Brain Metastases Undergoing Surgery

brief_summary:
Babies born extremely preterm (before 28 weeks of pregnancy) miss most of the transfer of two long-chain fatty acids, arachidonic acid (ARA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), that normally passes from mother to baby in the last three months of pregnancy. Low levels of these fatty acids after birth have been linked to retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), an eye disease that can threaten vision, and to other complications of prematurity. In a Swedish randomized trial (Mega Donna Mega), an enteral supplement of ARA and DHA reduced severe ROP by about half. A similar supplement, NeoMega36, is now used in routine care in several European neonatal units and is being introduced in Sweden.

This observational study examines whether the introduction of NeoMega36 into routine care is followed by less ROP and fewer other complications of prematurity. It compares infants born at 22+0 to 27+6 weeks of gestation who were cared for before NeoMega36 was introduced at their unit (historical period) with infants cared for after it was introduced (NeoMega period).

The study has two parts:

* European part: participating neonatal units report aggregated counts (number of infants and number with each outcome, by gestational week and period). No individual-level data leave the hospitals.
* Swedish part: coded individual-level data are retrieved from the Swedish Neonatal Quality Register (SNQ) and the Swedish national register for ROP (SWEDROP).

The study does not give, assign or change any treatment. NeoMega36 is given as part of routine clinical care according to each unit's own practice. There are no extra examinations, visits or contacts with families.

The main hypothesis is that the proportion of infants with severe ROP is lower in the NeoMega period than in the historical period. Other outcomes are treated ROP, any ROP, bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), death before discharge, and the combined outcomes BPD or death and NEC or death. Because this is a before-and-after comparison, differences between the periods may also reflect other changes in care over time, and the results will be interpreted with this in mind.
interventions: Enteral arachidonic acid and docosahexaenoic acid supplement
primary_outcomes: Severe retinopathy of prematurity (ROP)
title: Real-world Follow-up After Introduction of NeoMega36 Fatty-Acid Supplementation in Extremely Preterm Infants

brief_summary: This study will assess whether planned coronary angiography (CAG), and simple percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) when needed, can be completed safely and technically while participants are in a semi-sitting position with the head of the procedure table raised to 60 degrees. Ten clinically stable adults scheduled for an elective procedure are planned. The first stage will include participants undergoing CAG. After a safety review, the study may include participants expected to need only simple PCI. Heart rhythm, blood pressure, and blood oxygen will be monitored continuously. If predefined safety criteria occur, staff will lower the table or return the participant to a flat position and provide usual clinical care. Researchers will describe procedure completion, image quality, radiation exposure, contrast use, tolerance of the position, and safety events through 3 days after the procedure. This exploratory study is not designed to establish treatment efficacy.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With Coronary Angiography (CAG) Technical Success
Proportion of Participants With Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) Technical Success
Participants With Position-Related Serious Adverse Events or Prespecified Safety Events
title: Function-Friendly Semi-Fowler Positioning for Coronary Angiography and PCI

brief_summary: This study aims to compare the efficacy of preoperative oral diltiazem and oral propranolol in achieving controlled hypotension during functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS).
primary_outcomes: Incidence of hypotension
title: Preoperative Oral Diltiazim Versus Oral Propranolol for Preforming Induced Hypotension in Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery

brief_summary:
Musculoskeletal injuries and conditions requiring temporary immobilization or reduced loading can lead to rapid losses of muscle mass and strength. Blood flow restriction (BFR) is a rehabilitation technique that uses an inflatable cuff placed around the proximal part of an arm or leg to temporarily restrict blood flow. The BFR-AcuteRehab study aims to investigate whether adding BFR to conventional rehabilitation improves physical function and recovery compared with sham BFR (sBFR), which uses minimal cuff pressure.

This prospective, randomized, sham-controlled clinical study will include 210 adults aged 18-60 years with unilateral musculoskeletal injuries or conditions affecting the distal upper or lower extremity. Participants will be assigned to one of three predefined clinical cohorts: (1) distal forearm injuries or conditions requiring temporary immobilization or reduced loading (n = 66); (2) hand joint instability, including midcarpal instability (n = 66); and (3) distal lower-leg injuries or conditions requiring temporary immobilization or reduced loading (n = 78).

Within each cohort, participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to BFR or sham BFR. All participants will receive conventional physiotherapy and/or occupational therapy in addition to their allocated intervention.

For participants with distal forearm or distal lower-leg injuries or conditions, BFR or sham BFR will be applied passively, without concomitant exercise, two to three times per week for the duration of the immobilization or load-restriction period. Participants with hand joint instability will receive active BFR or sham BFR during conventional therapeutic exercises, two to three times per week for 12 weeks.

Assessments will be conducted at baseline (T0), at the end of the respective intervention period (T1), and approximately one year after baseline (T2). The primary outcomes are upper-extremity function, assessed using the Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand questionnaire (QuickDASH) in the two upper-extremity cohorts, and lower-extremity function, assessed using the Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS) in the distal lower-leg cohort.

Secondary outcomes include muscle strength, health-related quality of life, anthropometric measurements, body composition, ultrasound-derived muscle morphology, residual functional deficits, sick-leave duration, return-to-work status, and adverse events.

The study will evaluate whether BFR provides additional benefits to conventional rehabilitation in patients with musculoskeletal injuries or conditions of the distal upper and lower extremities.
interventions: Passive Blood Flow Restriction - Distal Forearm
Active Blood Flow Restriction - Hand Joint Instability
Active Sham Blood Flow Restriction - Hand Joint Instability
Passive Blood Flow Restriction - Distal Lower Leg
Passive Sham Blood Flow Restriction - Distal Lower Leg
primary_outcomes: Upper-Extremity Function (QuickDASH) - Distal Forearm Cohort
Upper-Extremity Function (QuickDASH) - Hand Joint Instability Cohort
Lower-Extremity Function (LEFS) - Distal Lower-Leg Cohort
title: Blood Flow Restriction Training in Acute Hospital Rehabilitation

brief_summary:
This clinical trial aims to investigate the development of and changes in fetal epigenetic signatures and how maternal metabolism influences these.

The metabolic profiles of the mother will be evaluated at three timepoints during pregnancy from a fasting blood sample and at another timepoints from an oral glucose tolerance test. Fetal epigenetic signatures can be identified by analyzing fetal cell-free DNA that circulates in the mother's bloodstream.
interventions: Metabolic and epigenetic characterization of mothers and fetuses
primary_outcomes: Epigenetic profiles of mothers and fetuses
Changes in epigenetic profiles of mothers and fetuses during pregnancy
title: Imprinting in Metabolic Diseases - Identifying Epigenetic Mechanisms in Human Gestational Diabetes Through Cell-free DNA - Part B

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether Andy's Mind, a psychoeducational card game co-created with a person with lived experience of psychosis, improves illness awareness (insight) and attitudes toward treatment in adults with schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders, compared with conventional group psychoeducation.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Andy's Mind improve insight into mental disorder more than conventional psychoeducation?
* Does Andy's Mind improve attitudes toward medication, as an indicator of treatment adherence, more than conventional psychoeducation?

Researchers will also look at psychotic symptoms, attitudes toward alcohol and other drugs, and participant satisfaction.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of two groups: the Andy's Mind game group or a conventional psychoeducation group.
* Attend 8 weekly group sessions of 45 minutes. Both groups cover the same topics: what psychosis is, symptoms, treatment, side effects, substance use and relapse prevention.
* Complete interviews and questionnaires before the sessions, right after the last session, and two months later.

The study takes place in mental health services in Catalonia, Spain, including prison mental health units, psychosocial rehabilitation services and community mental health centers.
conditions: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
primary_outcomes: Insight into mental disorder (Scale to Assess Unawareness of Mental Disorder, SUMD)
Attitudes toward antipsychotic medication as an indicator of treatment adherence (Drug Attitude Inventory, DAI-10)
title: Andy's Mind: A Co-created Serious Game for People With Psychosis (PSICOGAME)

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to find out the views of nurses and inpatients with type 2 diabetes of the Diabetes Insulin self-Management Education (DIME) web-based application. DIME was developed by nurses and people with type 2 diabetes, and a prototype was developed. The DIME app has been developed over a long period of time in response to the needs and concerns of people with type 2 diabetes starting insulin and a pilot study which led to the development of the original DIME programme. The current study involves introducing the DIME app to a small number of people starting insulin in hospital and the nurses who educate them and interviewing them about their thoughts on using it. The investigators will also count the number of people with type 2 diabetes who start insulin in hospital and the main reason for starting it over a 6 month period.

This project will help us to understand if a digital tool such as DIME might help to support in hospital insulin starts. The investigators will also know how many people are likely to need the support as they will have counted the number of people starting insulin when they have type 2 diabetes in hospital over a 6 month period. It will involve patients and nurses. The nurses involved will understand how, what, when, and why new technology such as the DIME app can fit within the hospital setting.

The study has been designed to address the following questions:

What are the views of people living with type 2 diabetes and nurses on the use of a web-based app to support in-hospital insulin starts? How many people with type 2 diabetes start insulin in hospital over a 6 month period and what is the reason for starting it?
primary_outcomes: views of DIME
title: Diabetes Insulin Self-Management Education (DIME) Web-based Application to Support People With Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) Starting Insulin in Hospital

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether locking peripheral venous catheters with heparin keeps them open (patent) better than locking them with saline, in adults admitted to hospital who have a peripheral venous catheter for intermittent treatment. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the percentage of blocked peripheral venous catheters higher in patients whose catheters are locked with saline than in those whose catheters are locked with heparin?
* Do the rates of other catheter-related complications (phlebitis, catheter-related bloodstream infection, extravasation, and leakage at the insertion site) differ between the two groups?
* Which clinical and drug-related factors are associated with catheter blockage?

Researchers will compare patients admitted to a hospital that routinely locks catheters with saline with patients admitted to a hospital that routinely locks catheters with heparin.
lead_sponsor: Consorci Sanitari de l'Alt Penedès i Garraf
primary_outcomes: Percentage of blocked peripheral venous catheters
title: Heparin Versus Saline Locking of Peripheral Venous Catheters

brief_summary:
Aortic stenosis (AS) is the most common valvular heart disease, and no medical therapy has been shown to slow its progression; treatment is limited to surgical or transcatheter aortic valve replacement once symptoms or left ventricular dysfunction develop. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization in patients with and without diabetes, and preclinical studies show that they suppress the inflammatory (NLRP3 inflammasome), fibrotic (TGF-beta/Smad), and oxidative-stress pathways that drive valve calcification. A recent observational study reported slower AS progression in patients treated with SGLT2 inhibitors.

SAVE-AS is a multicenter, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, investigator-initiated superiority trial testing whether the SGLT2 inhibitor enavogliflozin (0.3 mg once daily) reduces the composite of all-cause death, aortic valve replacement, and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with asymptomatic moderate or severe aortic stenosis and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (50% or higher). A total of 1,182 participants at 11 centers in the Republic of Korea will be randomized 1:1 to enavogliflozin or matching placebo, stratified by participating center and AS severity (moderate vs severe). Study treatment is given for 24 months, with follow-up visits at 2, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months and an end-of-treatment assessment at 25 months. Secondary outcomes include the individual components of the primary composite, cardiac death, echocardiographic AS severity, left ventricular mass, global longitudinal strain and ejection fraction, NT-proBNP, annual eGFR slope, and SGLT2 inhibitor-related adverse events. All clinical events are adjudicated by an independent clinical event adjudication committee, and safety is overseen by an independent data and safety monitoring board.
primary_outcomes: Composite of all-cause death, aortic valve replacement, or hospitalization for heart failure
title: SGLT2 Inhibitor in Patients With Asymptomatic Moderate or Severe Aortic Stenosis

brief_summary: The aim of this mixed method study is to evaluate a structured nurse-led patient education and tele-monitoring for asthma patients with suboptimal control.
interventions: Structured nurse-led patient education and tele-monitoring
primary_outcomes: Improvement of GINA scores
The frequency of asthma exacerbation
The frequency of asthma related visit to emergency department and hospitalization
title: Evaluation of a Structured Nurse-led Patient Education and Tele-monitoring to Review Asthma Patients With Suboptimal Control: A Pilot Study

brief_summary:
Physical frailty is a common health concern among older adults with hypertension and may contribute to reduced physical function, loss of independence, and poorer quality of life. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a 12-week nurse-led Physical Frailty Intervention Module (PFIM) among community-dwelling older adults with hypertension and physical frailty in Shandong Province, China.

This nonrandomized controlled study will recruit 124 participants aged 60 years or older from three primary healthcare institutions. Two institutions will be assigned to the intervention group, which will receive the PFIM in addition to usual care, while one institution will serve as the control group and provide usual care only.

The PFIM is based on the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA) and combines simplified Baduanjin exercise, basic nutrition guidance, hypertension self-management education, and behavioral support. The intervention includes nurse-led group sessions, individualized home-based exercise, and follow-up support over 12 weeks.

Physical frailty will be the primary outcome. Physical performance, nutritional status, health literacy, perceived social support, depressive symptoms, and quality of life will be assessed as secondary outcomes at baseline and after 12 weeks.
primary_outcomes: Change in Physical Frailty Severity Measured by the FRAIL Scale
title: Physical Frailty Intervention for Older Adults With Hypertension and Physical Frailty

brief_summary:
This study is looking at how a ketogenic diet (a way of eating that is high in fat and very low in carbohydrates) affects hormones, metabolism, and body composition in healthy women who have regular menstrual cycles. While ketogenic diets have become popular and have been studied in men and in people with certain health conditions, much less is known about how this way of eating affects the hormones and cycles of healthy, premenopausal women.

Researchers believe that a ketogenic diet may cause measurable changes in reproductive hormones (such as estrogen and progesterone), metabolic markers (like ketone and cholesterol levels), and body composition (such as body fat and lean muscle mass) across the menstrual cycle. The study will also explore whether the diet affects mood, sleep, and overall well-being.

Participants will follow a ketogenic diet for 12 weeks, roughly covering three menstrual cycles. During the first month, they will receive help with meal planning and food, and for the remaining weeks they will follow the diet on their own with continued support from a dietitian. Throughout the study, participants will check in weekly for blood draws, body composition scans, and a resting metabolism test, and will use at-home tools such as a smart ring and daily finger-stick tests to track their ketone levels and hormone patterns. Participants will also complete surveys about their mood, sleep, and general well-being.

By studying these changes closely, the research team hopes to better understand how a ketogenic diet affects women's health and hormones, which could help guide future dietary recommendations designed specifically for women.
primary_outcomes: Change in Ovulatory Status
title: How a Ketogenic Diet Affects Hormones and Metabolism in Women

brief_summary:
This study is the first step of a research programme on a new treatment for first responders with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD): couple therapy in which both partners take MDMA, under medical supervision, in three of fourteen sessions. The treatment is called Process-Centred MDMA-Assisted Couple Psychotherapy, or PACT-MDMA.

Current treatments help many people with PTSD, but many drop out or improve only in part, and few treatments work directly on the relationship, which PTSD strains and which can help recovery. MDMA-assisted therapy has been tested in large trials in the United States, but these studies' designs have been criticised, and the therapy component of the treatment has rarely been specified or measured. No Canadian study has tested MDMA-assisted therapy in first responders, and none has tested it with couples.

This feasibility study at the University of Ottawa will enrol six to ten couples in which one partner is a current or former first responder with PTSD. It asks whether the treatment can be delivered safely, whether couples can be recruited and kept in the study, and whether the sessions and measures work as planned. It does not aim to prove that the treatment works. Two exploratory hypotheses will be examined: that the partner with PTSD will show a reduction in clinician-rated PTSD severity from baseline to the end of treatment that is maintained six months later, and that the other partner will accommodate PTSD symptoms less while both partners report a better relationship over the same period.

A nurse is present and a physician on call during every MDMA session; all sessions are recorded so that the therapy can be checked for fidelity to its written principles; and the research, therapy and medical roles are kept separate. If this phase succeeds, a second phase would compare PACT-MDMA with standard PTSD therapy in about 24 couples in Ottawa and Montreal, and a third would extend the study to several Canadian sites.
primary_outcomes: Recruitment: number of couples screened, eligible and enrolled, and enrolment rate
Retention: proportion of enrolled couples completing the three treatment cycles and each assessment point
Protocol adherence: proportion of scheduled sessions completed per protocol, and protocol variations, deviations and stopping-rule events
Therapist fidelity to the PACT-MDMA model (PACT-MDMA Fidelity Rating Scale, PACT-FRS)
Safety: frequency, severity, seriousness and relatedness of adverse events
title: MDMA-Assisted Couple Psychotherapy for PTSD in First Responders: A Phase I Feasibility Study (PACT-MDMA)

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out whether thinking and memory ability (cognitive status) is related to the health of the gums and the bone around the teeth (periodontal health) in adults who visit a dental periodontology clinic. Gum disease is a long-lasting inflammation, and some studies suggest it may be linked to memory and thinking problems, but the strength and direction of this link are still unclear. Adults aged 18 and over who come for treatment to the Periodontology Department of Niğde Ömer Halisdemir University Faculty of Dentistry and who agree to take part will complete a short questionnaire and a memory and thinking test (the Mini-Mental State Examination). A periodontist will then measure gum pocket depth, attachment loss, plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding, and the number of missing teeth, and will review dental X-rays. About 220 people will take part. No new treatment will be given as part of this study. The results may help dentists understand how oral health and cognitive health are connected and may support future prevention strategies.
primary_outcomes: Cognitive status measured by Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) total score
title: Association Between Cognitive Status and Periodontal Parameters in Patients Attending a Periodontology Clinic

brief_summary: In this study, 48 individuals with shoulder impingement syndrome were divided into three groups to compare the effects of traditional physical therapy, traditional physical therapy combined with rigid taping, and kinesiology taping. After three weeks of treatment, significant improvements in muscle strength, pain, functionality, and joint position sense were observed in all groups. In a comparison between the groups, it was determined that rigid taping was more effective than traditional physical therapy in reducing pain, while both taping methods were more effective than traditional physical therapy in improving functionality and joint position sense. No significant difference was found between the groups in terms of muscle strength.
primary_outcomes: SPADI (Shoulder Pain and Disability İndex)
title: The Effects of Rigid and Kinesiological Taping, Applied as an Adjunct to Conventional Physical Therapy, on Muscle Strength, Pain, Function, and Joint Position Sense in Individuals With Shoulder Impingement Syndrome

brief_summary:
This study examined whether a brief, online self-compassion writing intervention could reduce shame and social anxiety in adults experiencing elevated levels of social anxiety and shame. Shame, or feeling negatively about oneself, is closely linked to social anxiety. Self-compassion, which involves responding to personal difficulties with kindness and understanding rather than self-criticism, may help reduce these experiences.

The main questions this study aimed to answer were:

1. Does a shame-focused self-compassion writing intervention increase self-compassion and reduce shame?
2. Does the intervention reduce social anxiety symptoms, avoidance, and negative patterns of thinking associated with social anxiety?
3. Are improvements maintained over time?

In this randomized controlled study, 94 adults were assigned to either a self-compassion writing intervention or a waitlist control group. Participants in the intervention group completed five online writing exercises over two weeks, focusing on responding to shame-related experiences with greater self-compassion. Participants completed questionnaires before the intervention, after two weeks, and at a one-month follow-up. Researchers compared changes between the two groups to evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Self-Compassion Scale (SCS) Score at Day 15 and One-Month Follow-Up
Change From Baseline in Experiences of Shame Scale (ESS) Score at Day 15 and One-Month Follow-Up
Change From Baseline in External and Internal Shame Scale (EISS) Total Score at Day 15 and One-Month Follow-Up
title: Effects of a Self-Compassion Intervention on Shame and Social Anxiety

brief_summary: This is a prospective, single-center, non-inferiority trial comparing a hospital-to-home transitional cardiac rehabilitation model with standard hospital-based cardiac rehabilitation in low-risk patients after cardiac surgery in Taiwan. Because patients' post-discharge scheduling constraints and treatment preferences make full randomization difficult to sustain in practice, the trial uses a Partially Randomized Patient Preference (PRPP) design: patients without a strong preference are randomized 1:1 to the two programs and form the randomized core cohort used for the primary confirmatory analysis, while patients with a clear, pre-specified preference are assigned accordingly and followed descriptively as a preference cohort. The primary hypothesis is that the hospital-to-home model is non-inferior to hospital-based rehabilitation in improving peak oxygen uptake (Peak VO2) after 8 weeks. A pre-specified key secondary hypothesis, based on an exploratory finding from the investigators' completed pilot study, is that the hospital-to-home model results in significantly lower 6-month outpatient medical costs. The trial does not include a no-treatment control arm; assay sensitivity is instead supported by the extensive existing evidence base for cardiac rehabilitation versus no treatment and for home-based versus center-based cardiac rehabilitation equivalence, following the constancy assumption described in ICH E10.
interventions: Standard center-based cardiac rehabilitation：as in Arm 2.
primary_outcomes: Change in Peak Oxygen Uptake (VO2peak) Measured by Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing
title: Home-Based Transitional Cardiac Rehabilitation Trial With a Partially Randomized Patient Preference Design

brief_summary:
This study examines the effects of an eye gel containing liposomal ozonated oil in middle-aged women with dry eye disease. Dry eye can cause discomfort, an unstable tear film, and inflammation of the eye surface.

The main questions are whether one week of treatment changes:

Tear film stability and other signs and symptoms of dry eye.

Markers of inflammation in cells collected from the eye surface.

Proteins involved in maintaining connections between eye surface cells.

Women with dry eye use the eye gel for one week and undergo assessments before and after treatment. These assessments include a symptom questionnaire, eye surface examinations, and collection of small samples of cells from the conjunctiva, the thin tissue covering the white of the eye.

A separate group of healthy young women undergoes one assessment without receiving treatment. Their measurements provide reference values for comparison with those of women with dry eye.

brief_summary:
Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease with systemic manifestations. Psoriatic arthritis is an important extracutaneous manifestation that can lead to progressive joint damage and functional disability if not recognized early.

Methotrexate remains a commonly used systemic therapy in both chronic plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis, mainly through anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects.
primary_outcomes: CAPN12 mRNA expression
title: CAPN12 Gene Expression as a Molecular Discriminator

brief_summary: This cross-sectional study aims to detect colistin heteroresistance phenotypically and genotypically among multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacilli isolated from clinical specimens at Assiut University Hospitals.

title: Colistin Heteroresistance in Multidrug-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacilli

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if larazotide acetate, which will be tested at two doses and compared to placebo, can help prevent signs and symptoms of celiac disease in patients with well-controlled celiac disease who are following a gluten-free diet. Both adults and children (ages 12 years and up) will be allowed to enroll in this study.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of responders treatment with larazotide acetate (0.25 mg or 0.5 mg) compared to placebo during the last two weeks of the 14-week treatment period
title: Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Protective Effect of Larazotide Acetate in Individuals With Well-Controlled Celiac Disease

brief_summary: This study was conducted to compare the effects of traditional oral motor therapy and app-based oral motor therapy in children with cerebral palsy. A randomised controlled trial design was used, and data was collected from children aged 6 to 12 years diagnosed with spastic cerebral palsy and oral motor difficulties. A standardised assessment tool (Not-s) was applied before and after intervention to evaluate changes in oral motor function. Data was collected from Fast rehab, Lahore. SPSS 26 was used for data entry and analysis. The results of this study are expected to provide better understanding of the effectiveness of app-based therapy compared to conventional approaches and support evidence-based rehabilitation strategies for children with cerebral palsy.
primary_outcomes: Nordic Orofacial Test-Screening
title: Effects of Traditional and App-based Oral Motor Therapy in Children With Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary: This multicenter, randomized, open-label clinical trial will enroll 360 adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD): 240 with stable COPD and 120 hospitalized with an acute exacerbation (AECOPD). Participants will be stratified by disease stage and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndrome. Within each syndrome stratum, they will be assigned to standardized Western medical treatment alone or the same treatment plus a syndrome-specific optimized herbal formula; selected strata will also include an innovative herbal formula group. Stable-phase participants will receive the study herbal treatment for 12 weeks, and AECOPD participants for 2 weeks. Both cohorts will be followed for 24 weeks. The study will assess lung function and exacerbations in stable COPD, and early dyspnea improvement and length of hospital stay in AECOPD. It will also assess symptoms, quality of life, TCM syndrome scores, safety, and biological markers.
conditions: Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

brief_summary: This work aimed to assess the hemodynamic effects of ketamine versus etomidate with or without midazolam as induction agents in patients undergoing emergency surgery.
primary_outcomes: Mean arterial pressure at 10 minutes
title: Optimal Induction Agent in Hemodynamically Unstable Patients Undergoing Emergency Surgery: A Comparative Study Between Ketamine and Etomidate With or Without Midazolam

brief_summary:
This is a decentralized, single-arm, within-subject crossover clinical study evaluating the effects of Driscoll's Raspberries and Driscoll's Blackberries on postprandial glycemic response, satiety, and consumer appeal in healthy adults aged 18-65 years. Forty participants will each consume three standardized breakfast meals - a raspberry-inclusive meal, a blackberry-inclusive meal, and a sugar-reference meal - in any order over a two-week period, wearing a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) throughout.

All study activities are conducted remotely at participants' homes. CGM data will be used to compute incremental area under the glucose-time curve (iAUC) over the two-hour postprandial window following each meal. Self-reported questionnaires will assess satiety, energy, digestive comfort, and sensory appeal following each meal condition.
primary_outcomes: Incremental Area Under the Glucose-Time Curve (iAUC) - Raspberry Meal vs. Sugar-Reference Meal
Incremental Area Under the Glucose-Time Curve (iAUC) - Blackberry Meal vs. Sugar-Reference Meal
title: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Effects of Driscoll's Raspberries and Driscoll's Blackberries on Postprandial Glycemic Response, Satiety, and Consumer Appeal in Healthy Adults

brief_summary: The main purpose of this study is to see if LY3839056 is safe and well tolerated when given as a single dose into a vein intravenous (IV) or under the skin subcutaneous (SC) in healthy participants. The study will also measure how much LY3839056 gets into the blood and how long it takes the body to remove it. The study will last up to 17 weeks and includes a stay of about 6 days at the clinical research unit.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the safety and tolerability of LY3839056 following single-dose administration (IV or SC) in healthy participants.
title: A Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of LY3839056 in Healthy Participants

brief_summary: Falls are a major health concern for adults with Intellectual Disabilities (ID), also termed as a Learning Disability (LD), with 30-60% experiencing at least one fall or 6.29 falls per person annually. It's the leading cause of injury and often results in fear of further falls, reduced mobility, lower engagement in physical activity (PA), and incidental loss of muscle mass. Adults with ID also experience higher gait and balance impairments, contributing to greater falls risk compared with the general population at a much younger age. Clinical guidelines recommend exercise as a first-line strategy for falls prevention. While many studies explore the use of technology in empowering physical activity, mainstream fitness research still excludes adults with Intellectual disabilities, limiting the applicability of current evidence of prevention exercises to this population. This research focuses specifically on adults with ID, which remains underdeveloped. This study, led by Physiotherapists, will test a digital tool in the form of the 'Physitrac' app with a tailored exercise program delivered through an easy-to-use patient-facing app (PhysiApp). This study will be recruiting adults with Intellectual disabilities from the NHS Greater Glasgow \& Clyde (GG\&C) health board area of Scotland, UK. This study will have two groups of patient and carer participants who will be randomly allocated using a computer software to follow a 12-week exercise program focused on improving strength, balance and overall physical activity. Strength and balance measurements will be recorded before and after the 12-week program, for patient participants, along with interviews with carer participants and Physiotherapists on their views of using the digital technology. This study will therefore evaluate the feasibility of the app in exercise delivery and explore whether digital data better supports exercise monitoring compared to usual care.

Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a multisystemic genetic disorder associated with frequent tumor, skin, visceral, and bone manifestations. Plexiform neurofibromas (PFNs), whether superficial or deep, affect 20 to 50 percent of patients and are responsible for significant morbidity. Inoperable, symptomatic PFNs can now be treated with targeted therapy (selumetinib) in both children and adults. Furthermore, NF1 patients frequently present with bone abnormalities, such as bone dysplasia, scoliosis, or reduced bone mineral density, suggesting impaired mineralization.

Inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) is a potent antagonist of bone mineralization. It has been shown in a mouse model of NF1 and in human Schwann cell cultures derived from patients with NF1 (2 cases) that there is activation of genes regulating PPi homeostasis, particularly ANKH and ENPP1.

This study aims to measure plasma PPi levels in a cohort of patients with NF1 from the general population, based on their phenotype-specifically, the presence, location, and characteristics of NFPs-as well as their calcium and phosphorus levels.

brief_summary:
Infections of the lungs are the most common problem for people with Cystic Fibrosis (CF), but also are significant in people with other lung conditions known generally as chronic suppurative lung diseases (CSLD), which can also cause recurrent chest infections. Some of the most common and severe infections are caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Pa), Staphylococcus aureus (Sa), and Aspergillus fumigatus (Af). It is important to detect these early, in order to treat them and prevent damage to the lungs.

At the moment we rely on sputum culture or cough swabs, however, some people (for example small children or those with less severe disease) are not able to provide sputum, and cough swabs are less accurate. Additionally, although modulators such as Kaftrio and Ivacaftor have had significant positive effects on most people with CF taking them, these people often find they no longer produce sputum, and therefore we are not able to test for infections in the same way we did before. Studies have shown that although some people have fewer infections after starting modulators, they generally don't disappear altogether, and therefore we still need a reliable way to test for them.

Furthermore, we have seen that some people react differently to certain infections, and people with more than one infection simultaneously, also respond differently to these infections.

We would like to find new, reliable, easy and acceptable ways of testing for infections that does not require sputum and are acceptable for patients in order to detect, monitor and treat lung infections early. Additionally, we would like to better understand what causes the differing responses patients have to infections, in order to see if there are new ways we can target treatments.

The study is being undertaken in multiple centres across the UK in order to recruit a larger, more diverse and representative group of participants, than we would be able to achieve from one centre alone.

title: The PRECISION Partners Platform (P3) Study

brief_summary:
Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) - polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and primary myelofibrosis - are characterized by excessive myeloid proliferation driven by mutations affecting the JAK2, CALR, and MPL genes, resulting in constitutive activation of hematopoietic cytokine signaling pathways. These hematological malignancies carry an increased risk of thrombosis and may evolve toward secondary myelofibrosis or acute leukemia. Bone marrow inflammation, particularly through interleukin-1 (IL-1), plays a major role in clonal expansion and the clinical expression of these diseases, as demonstrated by preclinical models showing the beneficial effect of its inhibition.

Anakinra, an IL-1 receptor antagonist widely used in rheumatology but never evaluated in MPNs, represents a promising therapeutic option. This proof-of-concept study will randomize 50 patients with a suboptimal response to cytoreductive therapy into two arms: anakinra 100 mg/day administered subcutaneously in combination with ongoing cytoreductive therapy (n=25), or cytoreductive therapy alone (n=25). The primary endpoint will be the reduction in serum calprotectin levels, a key inflammatory marker of the IL-1 loop that has recently demonstrated prognostic relevance in MPNs. Secondary endpoints will include improvements in hematological parameters, driver mutation allelic burden, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and quality of life.

This study represents an essential step toward larger trials aimed at demonstrating a durable reduction in thrombotic risk and disease progression.
primary_outcomes: Change in serum calprotectin levels
title: Interleukin-1 Inhibition to Improve the Response of Myeloproliferative Neoplasms Resistant to Cytoreductive Treatment

brief_summary:
The goal of the global Phase 1/2 clinical trial is to evaluate whether CID-103, a novel anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, is safe and effective in adults with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP). The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* To evaluate the safety and tolerability of CID-103 in subjects with ITP with different increasing doses of CID-103.
* To further evaluate the safety and tolerability of CID-103 at two or three dose levels and to select an optimal dose and administration regimen for CID-103 for further study of clinical efficacy.

The study will be done in two parts:

Part A will test increasing doses of CID-103 to see how safe it is and how well people tolerate it. Researchers will also aim to find a safe dose range.

Part B will compare up to three different doses of CID-103 to see how well the medicine works and gather more safety and efficacy information. The goal is to find the optimal dose to use in future studies.

CID-103 is given through an intravenous (IV) infusion. During the study, participants may receive treatment for up to 6 months, followed by a post-treatment safety follow-up period to check for ongoing safety and effectiveness.This study is an important step toward developing a new treatment for people living with chronic ITP. If CID-103 is found to be safe and effective, it could offer a new option for patients who do not respond well to current therapies.

brief_summary:
\*\*Study Summary\*\*

Hemodialysis patients frequently experience a high burden of dialysis-related symptoms, including fatigue, muscle weakness, pain, sleep disturbances, pruritus, and psychological complaints. These symptoms may negatively affect daily functioning and overall well-being. Intradialytic exercise has been proposed as a feasible complementary intervention to improve health-related outcomes in this population, as it allows patients to engage in physical activity during their routine hemodialysis sessions.

This study aims to investigate the effects of intradialytic aerobic exercise on dialysis-related symptoms and subjective well-being in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. A randomized controlled trial will be conducted involving patients receiving regular hemodialysis treatment. Participants will be randomly allocated to either an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group will perform intradialytic aerobic exercise using a pedal exercise device during hemodialysis sessions, while the control group will continue to receive standard hemodialysis care without an additional exercise intervention.

The intervention will be implemented over a six-week period, with exercise sessions conducted three times per week. Dialysis-related symptoms will be assessed using the Dialysis Symptom Index (DSI), while subjective well-being will be evaluated using the World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index (WHO-5). Both outcome measures will be administered before and after the intervention.

The primary objective is to determine whether intradialytic aerobic exercise reduces dialysis-related symptom burden compared with standard care. The secondary objective is to evaluate its effects on subjective well-being. The findings are expected to provide further evidence regarding the potential role of intradialytic aerobic exercise as a practical intervention for improving patient-centered outcomes in individuals receiving maintenance hemodialysis.
primary_outcomes: Dialysis Symptom Index (DSI)
title: Intradialytic Exercise, Symptoms, and Well-being in Hemodialysis Patients

A total of 92 adult patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting or heart valve surgery will be included. Participants will be randomly assigned to an intervention group (n=46) or a control group (n=46) using stratified block randomization based on surgical procedure.

Both groups will receive standard postoperative care, including breathing exercises, chest percussion, and incentive spirometry. brief_summary:
The aim of this study will be to evaluate the effect of reduced enamel etching time on the 6, 12, 18 and 24-months clinical performance of two universal adhesive systems used as etch-and-rinse application mode in non-carious cervical lesions (NCCLs).

Materials \& Methods: 140 restorations will be randomly placed in 35 subjects according to the following groups: AUP5 (Ambar Universal APS Plus adhesive on enamel etched for 5 seconds); AUP15 (Ambar Universal APS Plus adhesive on enamel etched for 15 seconds); SUB5 (Solare Universal Bond adhesive on enamel etched for 5 seconds); SUB15 (Solare Universal Bond adhesive on enamel etched for 15 seconds). All groups will be light-cured for 10s/1,000 mW/cm2. A resin composite will be placed by applying three increments and each one will be light cured for 20s/1,000 mW/cm2. Existing studies have confirmed that there are differences in the methylation status of liver tissue due to hepatitis B virus infection and alcohol consumption. There are also differences in the methylation status at each stage of the disease progression from hepatitis to liver cirrhosis and then to liver cancer. However, no study has systematically compared the cfDNA methylation profiles of hepatitis B subjects under different alcohol consumption statuses. Plasma cfDNA methylation detection has been proven to be applicable for the early warning of HBV - related liver cancer and has the characteristics of being non - invasive and allowing dynamic monitoring. However, most of the existing markers focus on the "liver cancer transformation" stage, and there is a lack of typing markers suitable for the early stage of "hepatitis progression". To preliminarily explore this field, this project was initiated.

This study is an observational and exploratory study that does not involve clinical treatment intervention for the subjects. The project plans to enroll 85 subjects with chronic hepatitis B. They will be divided into a non - drinking group, a drinking group, and a group that has developed alcoholic hepatitis due to alcohol consumption according to the degree of alcohol consumption. For each patient, 2 tubes of peripheral blood (about 8 mL per tube), a total of about 16 mL, will be collected for cfDNA methylation analysis. By comparing the plasma cfDNA methylation profiles of chronic hepatitis B subjects with different degrees of alcohol consumption, the impact of different degrees of alcohol consumption on the cfDNA methylation of the subjects will be analyzed.
