brief_summary:
Background and Objective Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after elective colorectal surgery and are associated with prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity, and delayed recovery. Existing PPC prediction tools were mainly developed in thoracic or mixed surgical populations and rely predominantly on clinical variables; preoperative chest CT information remains underused, and a population-specific tool for elderly colorectal cancer patients is still lacking. This study aims to develop and validate a multimodal deep learning model that integrates preoperative chest CT-derived features with multidimensional clinical variables to predict PPCs in patients aged ≥65 years undergoing elective radical colorectal cancer surgery, and to quantify its incremental value and clinical net benefit.

Methods This is a single-center retrospective cohort study. Eligible patients will be assigned to a development window (August 2020-August 2024), split chronologically at a 7∶1∶2 ratio into training, validation, and test sets with five-fold cross-validation, and a locked temporal external validation window (September 2024-September 2026), which will be used only after the final model is fixed. The primary outcome is 30-day composite PPCs defined according to the EPCO criteria; the Melbourne Group Scale will serve as a parallel sensitivity definition. Preoperative clinical variables and chest CT images obtained within four weeks before surgery will be collected. A convolutional neural network imaging branch-or 2D transfer learning based on RadImageNet if the sample size is insufficient-will extract CT deep features, which will be fused with clinical variables at the feature (intermediate) level. Six classifiers, including logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and multilayer perceptron, will be tuned within a unified search space. Discrimination (AUC with DeLong test and Bootstrap 95% CI), calibration (calibration curves, Brier score), incremental value (NRI, IDI), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis) will be evaluated against the ARISCAT and GSU-Pulmonary scores, a clinical-only model, and an imaging-only model. Grad-CAM and SHAP will be applied to interpret the model.

Expected Outcome The study is expected to provide an interpretable and deployable preoperative risk stratification tool for elderly patients undergoing colorectal surgery, clarify the incremental contribution of preoperative chest CT information, and define the threshold range in which the model yields net clinical benefit.
lead_sponsor: General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University
primary_outcomes: PPCs within 30 days after surgery
title: Multimodal Deep Learning Based on Chest CT and Clinical Features for Predicting the Risk of Postoperative Pulmonary Complications: A Decision Curve Analysis

Since 2018 (and 2023 for moderate hemophilia A), subcutaneous prophylactic treatment with emicizumab has drastically reduced bleeding episodes and, consequently, the frequency of IV infusions. However, IV injections remain necessary to treat acute breakthrough bleeds. The investigators hypothesize that previously autonomous patients or family caregivers may experience a gradual loss of skill and self-efficacy in performing IV injections while on emicizumab prophylaxis.

brief_summary:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, the most common type of pancreatic cancer, is treated when it arises in the head of the pancreas and can be removed by an operation called pancreaticoduodenectomy (the Whipple operation), followed by chemotherapy. Even after this operation the cancer returns in most patients. One important reason is that microscopic cancer cells are often left at the cut edges of the removed tissue, especially at the edge facing the superior mesenteric artery, the main artery that supplies the intestine. The tissue in this area, behind the head of the pancreas, is called the mesopancreas. It contains fat, lymph vessels, lymph nodes and nerves, through which pancreatic cancer commonly spreads.

Total mesopancreas excision is a refinement of the standard operation. The surgeon removes the whole mesopancreas in one piece together with the head of the pancreas by dissecting directly along the right side of the superior mesenteric artery, in the same way that the whole fatty envelope of the rectum is removed in rectal cancer surgery. Studies that compared patients operated on with and without this technique suggest that it may leave fewer cancer cells behind and reduce the chance of the cancer returning in the operated area, without increasing complications. Those studies were not randomized, however, so it is still unknown whether the technique itself is responsible for these benefits.

In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 110 adults with removable (resectable) cancer of the head of the pancreas will be assigned by chance, during the operation and after the surgeon has confirmed that the tumor can be removed, to pancreaticoduodenectomy with total mesopancreas excision or to standard pancreaticoduodenectomy. Patients, and the doctors who examine the removed tissue and the follow-up scans, will not be told which operation was performed. The main question is whether total mesopancreas excision increases the proportion of patients in whom no cancer cells are found within 1 mm of any cut edge (an R0 resection). The trial will also compare complications, diarrhea, recovery, the number of lymph nodes removed, the chance and pattern of cancer recurrence, survival and quality of life over 2 years of follow-up.
primary_outcomes: R0 Resection Rate (Tumor Clearance of 1 mm or More at All Resection Margins)

Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability in adults. Many people who have had a stroke continue to experience difficulty walking because of muscle weakness and spasticity, which can limit their mobility and quality of life.

Botulinum toxin injections are commonly used to reduce spasticity in specific muscles, such as the calf muscles. Rehabilitation is then used to improve walking ability. Robot-assisted gait rehabilitation allows patients to practice walking intensively and repeatedly, with assistance adjusted to their needs. Previous research from our team has shown that robot-assisted gait rehabilitation may improve walking ability more than conventional physical therapy when combined with botulinum toxin injections.

The purpose of this study is to better understand why robot-assisted gait rehabilitation may be more effective than conventional gait rehabilitation after botulinum toxin treatment in people with chronic stroke. The study will examine changes in walking patterns, muscle activity, and brain activity during and after rehabilitation. Brain activity and brain connections will be assessed using non-invasive methods, including functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electroencephalography (EEG), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

The study may help identify how the brain and body adapt to rehabilitation and may contribute to developing more personalized rehabilitation programs for people living with long-term effects of stroke.

* What is the level of interoceptive sensitivity (how participants self-report their awareness of body signals), as measured by the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness, Version 2 (MAIA-2), in each of the three groups?

In each group, researchers will also explore whether interoceptive accuracy and sensitivity are associated with:

* socio-demographic and clinical characteristics (gender, age, body mass index, illness duration, and IQ)

* Fill in the MAIA-2 questionnaire about body awareness, along with other questionnaires about eating behaviors, emotions, and general well-being

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a new way of adjusting heart failure medicines can improve health in adults with heart failure who live in rural areas. This study tests whether remotely helping local doctors safely raise these doses faster can improve health over the first 3 months after leaving the hospital.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the new approach help participants live longer, avoid needing a heart transplant or heart pump, stay out of the hospital for heart failure, and feel better day to day, over 6 months?
* Do more participants take all their recommended heart failure medicines, at the best doses, by 6 months?
* Does the new approach improve quality of life and daily activity, and how well does it work in everyday rural health care?

Participants will be placed by chance, like flipping a coin, into 1 of 2 groups: home monitoring alone or home monitoring plus medication optimization support. In the home monitoring alone group, participants' own doctors will manage their medicines as usual. In the medicine support group, heart failure specialists on the study team will use home readings and results from NT-proBNP blood tests, to send medicine advice to participants' own doctors. Researchers will compare the 2 groups to see if medicine support improves health and quality of life.

Participants will:

* Use a scale, blood pressure cuff, and activity tracker at home for 3 months
* May have routine blood tests ordered by their own doctor about 2 and 6 weeks after joining, if they are in the medicine support group
* Complete video or phone study visits when they join, at 3 months, and at 6 months
* Answer questions about their heart failure symptoms and quality of life at each visit
* Some participants may also be asked to take part in an interview about their experience.
primary_outcomes: Hierarchical Composite of All-Cause Mortality, Heart Transplantation or Ventricular-Assist Device, Heart Failure Hospitalizations, and Improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Score
title: Leveraging Telemedicine to Improve Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Use and Outcomes Among Rural Patients With Heart Failure

brief_summary: Infantile colic is a common condition characterized by excessive, inconsolable crying in otherwise healthy infants, and it can disrupt infant sleep and family well-being. Abdominal (colic) massage is a low-cost, non-pharmacological method that may help relieve colic symptoms, but evidence remains limited. This randomized controlled trial aims to determine the effect of colic massage applied by mothers on colic severity, crying duration and sleep duration in infants aged 2-12 weeks diagnosed with infantile colic according to Rome IV criteria. Mothers in the intervention group will be trained in colic massage and will apply it twice daily for 21 days; infants in the control group will continue routine care.
primary_outcomes: Colic Severity
title: Effect of Colic Massage on Colic Severity, Crying and Sleep in Infants With Infantile Colic

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized, parallel-group study aims to evaluate the additional effects of active Balancing Cream compared with its vehicle during a standardized series of five PRX S treatments in adults with mild-to-moderate facial acne.

A total of 50 participants aged 18-60 years with dermatologist-confirmed mild-to-moderate facial acne (Investigator's Global Assessment \[IGA\] grade 2 or 3) will be enrolled and allocated to two groups of 25 participants each.

Both groups will receive five PRX S treatments at 14-day intervals and use the same Nourishing Cream for Normal and Combination Skin in the morning. In the evening, the experimental group will apply active Balancing Cream containing azelaic acid, salicylic acid, and niacinamide, while the comparator group will use a corresponding cream vehicle without these three ingredients.

The primary outcome is the change from baseline in the total number of facial inflammatory lesions (papules and pustules), assessed two weeks after the fifth PRX S treatment. Secondary assessments include acne severity, non-inflammatory lesion counts, skin biophysical and imaging measurements, and treatment safety.

Clinical and instrumental assessments will be performed at baseline (T0), approximately day 42 (T1), approximately day 70 (T2), and two months after T2 (T3).

The study is designed to assess the additional benefit of active Balancing Cream compared with its vehicle under identical PRX S treatment conditions, rather than the independent efficacy of PRX S.
interventions: Nourishing Cream for Normal and Combination Skin
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Facial Inflammatory Lesion Count
title: Active Versus Vehicle Home Care During PRX S Treatment for Mild-to-Moderate Facial Acne

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the incidence of incisional hernia, detected by ultrasound imaging, two years after surgery in patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) undergoing either open or minimally invasive abdominal surgery with the use of prophylactic Phasix™ Mesh reinforcement. The study focuses on consecutive adult patients aged 18 years or older with a confirmed histological diagnosis of Crohn's disease or Ulcerative Colitis who are scheduled for elective abdominal surgery, specifically minimally invasive surgery requiring a periumbilical incision for specimen extraction or open abdominal surgery via a midline incision for patients undergoing their second or subsequent abdominal operation for IBD. The main questions it aims to answer are: what is the rate of 24-month incisional hernia as diagnosed by ultrasound imaging in the prospective study population, and how do secondary outcomes such as postoperative pain, quality of life, surgical site occurrences, and 90-day complication rates compare across these surgical strata? If there is a comparison group: Researchers will compare participants who received open surgery to those who received minimally invasive surgery to see if there are significant differences in the 24-month incisional hernia rates, complication profiles, and recovery metrics. Participants will undergo their planned abdominal surgery according to standard institutional care pathways, during which the study device-the Phasix™ Mesh-will be positioned to reinforce either the periumbilical extraction site in minimally invasive procedures or the midline incision in open surgeries using a standardized onlay technique. Following surgery, participants will be asked to complete a series of main tasks and evaluations, which include providing daily self-reported pain ratings on a Visual Analog Scale during hospitalization, attending scheduled follow-up visits at 30 days, 6 months, 12 months, and 24 months post-surgery, undergoing clinical evaluations and wound inspections with standardized photographic documentation at each visit, completing validated questionnaires including the Short-Form Health Survey-36, Ventral Hernia Pain Questionnaire, and Carolinas Comfort Scale at specified postoperative time points, and undergoing delegated ultrasound imaging of the entire length of the incision in both supine resting and dynamic states during the 12-month and 24-month follow-up visits to detect any occult or overt fascial defects or herniation.
primary_outcomes: the rate of 24-month incisional hernia
title: Prophylactic Phasix™ Mesh for Incisional Hernia Prevention in IBD Surgery: A Prospective Multicenter Study

brief_summary:
This study will compare two types of acupuncture for adults with mild to moderate depression. One group will receive acupuncture. The other group will receive pivot acupuncture, a technique that uses needles at points on the head and neck. Participants with depression will be assigned to one of the two groups by chance. Both groups will attend three sessions a week for six weeks.

The researchers will compare how many people in each group have a substantial improvement in their depression symptoms by the end of treatment. They will also use brain scans and blood tests to examine whether symptom improvement is related to changes in how different parts of the brain work together and to changes in blood levels of a protein called the sigma-1 receptor.
lead_sponsor: Shenzhen Hospital of Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With a Clinical Response on the HAMD-17
title: Acupuncture for Depression: Sigma-1 Receptor-Related Brain Network Modulation

brief_summary: This retrospective study aims at investigating the value of preoperative magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) in assessing the biomechanical characteristics of vestibular schwannomas and predicting surgical risk. Tumor stiffness and three-dimensional adhesion characteristics will be quantitatively analyzed and correlated with clinical parameters, including intraoperative tumor consistency and adhesion severity, operative time, blood loss, and postoperative neurological function. The study aims to validate the associations between MRE-derived imaging parameters, intraoperative findings, and clinical outcomes, thereby providing an imaging-based foundation for preoperative risk assessment and individualized surgical planning for vestibular schwannomas.
primary_outcomes: Association of Preoperative MRE-Derived Quantitative Parameters With Intraoperative Tumor Consistency and Adhesion Severity
title: Mechanical Characterization of Vestibular Schwannoma: Classification Based on Magnetic Resonance Elastography and Its Clinical Relevance Study

primary_outcomes: Incidence, severity, and causality of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs)
title: Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetic Study of Single and Multiple Ascending Dose of YY524051 Tablets in Healthy Adults.

brief_summary:
This study was conducted to compare a test formulation of dapagliflozin/metformin extended-release tablets (10 mg/1000 mg) with the reference product, XIGDUO XR, in healthy Chinese adults.

The main purpose was to determine whether the two products deliver similar amounts of dapagliflozin and metformin into the bloodstream at a similar rate.

The study included separate groups of participants who received the medications under fasting conditions or fed conditions. In each group, participants received both the test and reference products on separate occasions, with a washout period between treatments.

Blood samples were collected at scheduled times to measure the concentrations of dapagliflozin and metformin. The safety and tolerability of both products were also assessed .

The results were used to evaluate whether the test and reference products were bioequivalent under fasting and fed conditions.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether NeuroSync (Turkish: Nörosenkron), a 6-week, home-based, web-delivered auditory-cognitive training program, improves listening in noise in adults aged 18 to 65 years who use hearing aids in both ears for sensorineural hearing loss.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does NeuroSync training improve speech understanding in noise, measured with the Turkish Hearing in Noise Test (HINT)?
* Does NeuroSync training reduce listening effort, measured with a dual-task test?

Researchers will compare NeuroSync training with an active control condition (watching "how-to" videos on the same web platform) to see whether the training leads to greater improvement.

Participants will:

* Be assigned by chance to the NeuroSync training group or the video (active control) group
* Complete 4 sessions per week for 6 weeks at home (24 sessions, each up to 30 minutes), while continuing their usual daily hearing aid use
* Visit their hearing aid center before and after the 6-week period for hearing, listening-in-noise, and listening-effort tests and a questionnaire
primary_outcomes: Change in Speech Reception Threshold in Noise on the Turkish Hearing in Noise Test (HINT)
title: NeuroSync Auditory-Cognitive Training for Listening in Noise in Hearing Aid Users

brief_summary:
Fluid resuscitation is a cornerstone of sepsis management. However, to avoid unnecessary fluid loading, it is important to assess fluid responsiveness, ideally without administering additional fluids. The PEEP test may offer a means of predicting fluid responsiveness by inducing a transient increase in cardiac preload through a temporary reduction in intrathoracic pressure, without requiring a fluid bolus.

This study evaluated whether the positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) test could predict fluid responsiveness in mechanically ventilated patients with sepsis.

In this prospective, single-center study, 60 mechanically ventilated patients with sepsis were enrolled when their treating clinicians had independently planned a fluid challenge. Before the fluid challenge, patients underwent an end-expiratory occlusion test (EEOT) followed by a PEEP test. During the PEEP test, PEEP was temporarily reduced from a baseline level of ≥10 cmH2O to 5 cmH2O for one minute, and changes in cardiac index (CI) were recorded. Fluid responsiveness was defined as an increase in CI of at least 10% following a 300 mL crystalloid fluid challenge.

The primary objective was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of the PEEP test for predicting fluid responsiveness. Additional analyses evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the PEEP test in subgroups defined by baseline respiratory system compliance (Crs) and driving pressure (DP), and examined the relationships between PEEP test-induced changes in Crs and DP and the corresponding change in CI.
lead_sponsor: Bakirkoy Dr. Sadi Konuk Research and Training Hospital
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy of the PEEP Test for Predicting Fluid Responsiveness
title: Prediction of Fluid Responsiveness Using the PEEP Test in Patients With Sepsis

As a secondary objective several factors affecting the radiation exposure is also noted.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence (AI) program that analyzes color fundus photographs (CFP) taken during routine eye care in hospital clinics.

The main question it aims to answer is: What is the diagnostic performance of the AI program for eye diseases? Participants were patients attending the eye clinics of a hospital in Beijing, China, who had CFPs taken as part of their usual care. Participants did not have any extra tests or visits for research purposes. The AI program analyzed these photographs automatically, but its results were not shown to doctors or patients and did not change any part of their care. Researchers analyzed the AI results using records with names and other identifying information removed.

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to compare the efficacy of visual, verbal, and auditory gait retraining cues for reducing ground contact time in healthy active-duty service members during overground running and to assess participants' perceptual responses to each cue. primary_outcomes: Ground contact time
title: Ground Contact Time Gait Retraining

brief_summary: Transversalis fascia plane (TFP) block is an ultrasound-guided abdominal wall block used for postoperative analgesia after inguinal hernia repair. Perineural dexamethasone prolongs analgesia in peripheral nerve blocks, but its efficacy in fascial plane blocks, where the injectate reaches the nerves by diffusion, is uncertain, and no placebo-controlled randomized trial has addressed this question for the TFP block. This prospective, randomized, controlled, double-blind trial will evaluate whether adding 4 mg dexamethasone to bupivacaine in a TFP block prolongs the time to first analgesic request and reduces rescue analgesic consumption in adult patients undergoing elective unilateral open inguinal hernia repair under spinal anesthesia. Sixty-four patients will be randomized 1:1 to bupivacaine + dexamethasone or bupivacaine + saline.
primary_outcomes: Time to first analgesic request
title: Dexamethasone Added to Transversalis Fascia Plane Block in Inguinal Hernia Repair

brief_summary:
This study compares two ways of pacing the heart in adults with atrioventricular block, a condition in which electrical signals do not pass normally from the upper to the lower heart chambers. Participants must need a permanent pacemaker and have a left ventricular ejection fraction of at least 50% before implantation. Ejection fraction measures how much blood the main pumping chamber ejects with each beat.

The study will include 150 participants at Sheba Medical Center. By chance, 50 participants will receive conduction system pacing, which aims to stimulate the heart through its natural electrical conduction system, and 100 will receive conventional right ventricular pacing. Participants and treating clinicians will know which treatment is used.

The main question is whether the two pacing strategies differ in heart pumping function 24 months after implantation, taking the starting measurement into account. Researchers will also compare quality of life, heart-related emergency visits and hospitalizations, complications, pacemaker and lead function, repeat procedures, and use of healthcare resources.

Heart pumping function will be measured before implantation and at 12 and 24 months. Participants will complete the AQUAREL quality-of-life questionnaire before implantation and at 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months. Device follow-up will include routine clinical care and remote monitoring.
primary_outcomes: Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction at 24 Months
title: Conduction System Pacing Versus Conventional Right Ventricular Pacing in Adults With Atrioventricular Block

brief_summary: This is a Phase 1 feasibility study evaluating the safety, barrier efficacy, and user acceptability of a novel male contraceptive device, the Galactic Cap (GC), an adhesive, polyurethane-based barrier designed to cover the glans penis. Unlike traditional condoms, the device adheres directly to the penile surface to improve fit, reduce slippage, and enhance sensation through increased skin-to-skin contact and improved heat transfer. The study will enroll 40 monogamous heterosexual couples in which the male partner has undergone vasectomy, allowing assessment of device performance independent of pregnancy risk. Participants will use the device during four separate acts of vaginal intercourse over approximately one month, with data collected via genital examinations, participant diaries, post-use surveys, and pre- and post-coital vaginal swabs analyzed for prostate-specific antigen (PSA) to assess semen leakage. The primary objective is to evaluate safety, with secondary assessment of barrier effectiveness and exploratory evaluation of device performance and user satisfaction compared to traditional condoms.

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether the gut bacteria of adults with inflammatory or immune-mediated skin diseases differ from those of healthy adults. It will include people with atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, vitiligo, alopecia areata, acne, pemphigus, or bullous pemphigoid, as well as healthy controls.

Participants will provide a stool sample and complete a short food diary. The study team will analyze the bacteria in the samples and compare the results between the disease groups and healthy controls. Participants with a skin disease will be asked to provide a second stool sample and complete follow-up assessments about six months later; healthy controls will provide one sample. The study will also examine whether changes in gut bacteria are related to skin disease severity, diet, and other collected health information.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda, Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico
primary_outcomes: Relative abundance of Bifidobacteriaceae in stool
title: Gut Microbiome Diversity in Adults With Inflammatory and Immune-Mediated Skin Diseases

brief_summary:
Typical absence seizures are the hallmark of idiopathic generalized epilepsy syndromes (CAE, JAE, JME) but are frequently underreported in patient diaries. Clinical studies have shown that 74% to 94% of absence seizures go unreported by patients or caregivers. While 24-hour video-EEG (vEEG) is the gold standard for quantification, it is expensive, hospital-based, and lacks the temporal resolution required for long-term management.

Previous studies successfully validated a wearable EEG (wEEG) solution using a behind-the-ear (BTE) form factor (Byteflies Sensor Dot). In the pilot study, the authors demonstrated that a reduced electrode configuration combined with ML algorithms could detect absence seizures with 98% sensitivity in the hospital setting and enable effective home-based treatment monitoring.

To expand the applicability of this method, validation of additional form factors is required. This study aims to extend our validation framework to a novel wEEG device that utilizes an ear configuration (earEEG).
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity (Recall)
Precision
F1-score
False Alarm Rate in 24 hours
title: Portable Absence Seizure Detection Using Smart Earbuds

brief_summary: This project aims to implement and assess the efficacy of a culturally adapted, individual Motivational Interviewing (MI)-based intervention for justice-involved people in Portugal: the Portuguese Version of the Short Motivational Programme (SMP-PV). This mixed-methods study will involve a randomized controlled trial (RCT) and aims to: (a) assess the efficacy of the SMP-PV in improving motivation for change (primary outcome) and therapeutic alliance and reducing blame attribution, and criminogenic cognitions (secondary outcomes); (b) examine whether changes are maintained at three and six months following completion of the SMP-PV; (c) assess the program's acceptability; and (d) evaluate the quality of MI practice within the SMP-PV. The sample will include Portuguese men and women, over 18 years old, serving prison sentences. Participants will be assessed at four time-points using self-report questionnaires, and post-treatment interviews will be conducted to gather their perceptions regarding the program. A final evaluation will be conducted to assess the quality and integrity of MI implementation, as well as the performance of the psychologist, by two independent coders using the Motivational Interviewing Treatment Integrity 4.2.1 Manual.
primary_outcomes: Motivation for Change (University of Rhode Island Change Assessment Scale and Change Questionnaire)
title: Effectiveness of the Portuguese Version of the Short Motivational Programme (SMP-PV) With Justice-Involved People

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare two types of plates used to surgically treat olecranon fractures, which are fractures of the bony point of the elbow. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a plate that preserves the triceps tendon result in better triceps strength than a plate that requires splitting the triceps tendon?
* Are there differences in elbow movement and function between the two treatments?

Researchers will compare participants treated with a short-flange plate that preserves the triceps tendon with participants treated with a long-flange plate that requires splitting the triceps tendon.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two surgical treatment groups
* Undergo surgical fixation of their olecranon fracture using the assigned plate
* Have their elbow strength and range of motion measured during follow-up
* Complete questionnaires about arm function, elbow function, general health, and pain during follow-up
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Triceps Strength
title: Triceps Strength Following Olecranon Fracture Fixation

brief_summary:
Background and Rationale Cytomegalovirus (CMV) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in recipients of solid organ transplantation (SOT) and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Current management relies on antiviral prophylaxis or pre-emptive therapy guided primarily by CMV-DNAemia monitoring. However, recently introduced antivirals such as letermovir and maribavir have changed the virological profile of CMV infection, highlighting limitations of DNAemia as a marker of active viral replication and increasing the need for improved resistance monitoring.

Preliminary studies suggest that CMV-RNAemia (UL21.5 mRNA) may be a more accurate marker of active viral replication and may detect viral clearance approximately 7-14 days earlier than CMV-DNAemia. In parallel, Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) may provide superior detection of antiviral resistance mutations, including low-frequency variants that cannot be identified by conventional Sanger sequencing.

Primary Objective To determine whether using CMV-RNAemia to guide discontinuation of antiviral therapy in transplant recipients can reduce treatment duration and drug-related toxicity without increasing the risk of CMV relapse, compared with the current standard based on CMV-DNAemia.

Secondary Objectives

Compare the diagnostic performance of NGS and Sanger sequencing in detecting CMV antiviral resistance mutations.

Estimate the incidence of resistant or refractory CMV infection (R/R-CMV) in transplant recipients.

Identify risk factors associated with the development of R/R-CMV according to transplant type.

Study Design This is a single-center, pragmatic, randomized controlled interventional study conducted at the IRCCS Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna.

Adult transplant recipients (≥18 years) with CMV infection requiring antiviral therapy will be randomized (1:1) into two groups:

Experimental arm: antiviral therapy discontinued after two consecutive negative CMV-RNAemia results.

Control arm: antiviral therapy discontinued after two consecutive negative CMV-DNAemia results.

Patients will be followed from treatment initiation, with virological monitoring continuing during therapy and follow-up.

Population and Sample Size The study plans to enroll approximately 330 CMV infection episodes, including an estimated 10% drop-out rate, with 150 participants per study arm plus additional cases to compensate for losses.

Endpoints Primary endpoints include:

Time to treatment discontinuation. Time to viral clearance. Incidence and timing of clinically significant CMV relapse. Antiviral drug toxicity.

Secondary endpoints include:

Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive value of NGS versus Sanger sequencing. Incidence of resistant/refractory CMV infection. Identification of clinical and virological risk factors for resistance.

Resistance Analysis In suspected resistant or refractory CMV infections, residual biological samples will undergo NGS analysis targeting CMV genes involved in antiviral resistance (UL97, UL54, UL56, UL89, UL27, UL51). Results will be compared with standard Sanger sequencing to assess earlier detection of resistance mutations and minor viral variants.

Expected Impact The study aims to establish CMV-RNAemia as a clinically useful marker for earlier identification of viral clearance, enabling shorter antiviral treatment and reduced toxicity. It also seeks to validate NGS-based resistance testing as a more sensitive tool for detecting emerging CMV drug resistance, ultimately supporting a more personalized approach to CMV management in transplant recipients and potentially other immunocompromised populations.

Study Duration and Funding The study is expected to last 24 months (18 months recruitment, 4 months follow-up, 2 months analysis) and is funded by the Italian Ministry of Health (Ricerca Corrente 2026, project RC-2026-2802099).
primary_outcomes: CMV-DNAemia VS CMV-DNAemia 1
CMV-DNAemia VS CMV-DNAemia 2
CMV-DNAemia VS CMV-DNAemia 3
CMV-DNAemia VS CMV-DNAemia 4
title: Cytomegalovirus Infection After Transplantation: a Study of New Markers to Optimize the Selection of Antiviral Therapies and Reduce the Risk of Developing Direct and Indirect Infection-related Complications

Specifically, the study will investigate the effects of these exercises on preoperative and postoperative anxiety levels, pain intensity scores, nausea and vomiting scores, time to mobilization (hours), total length of hospital stay (hours), and patient satisfaction.

title: The Effects of Virtual Reality-Based Relaxation on Postoperative Symptoms and Patient Satisfaction Among Adolescents Undergoing Emergency Surgery

brief_summary:
Osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) of the talus is a condition affecting the bone and cartilage of the ankle joint. It can cause pain, swelling, stiffness, and difficulty participating in sports and daily activities. Children and adolescents with persistent symptoms or unstable lesions may require surgery when nonsurgical treatments are unsuccessful.

Two surgical approaches used to treat this condition are arthroscopic drilling and chondroplasty, which aim to stimulate healing of the affected bone and cartilage, and viable cartilage allograft implantation, which uses donated cartilage material to repair the damaged area. There is limited evidence comparing these treatments in children and adolescents, and it is not known whether one approach provides better outcomes.

This pilot randomized controlled trial aims to assess the feasibility of conducting a larger study comparing these two surgical treatments in pediatric patients with talar OCD. Approximately 20 participants requiring surgery will be recruited at the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (CHEO) and randomly assigned to receive either viable cartilage allograft implantation (CartiMax®) or arthroscopic drilling and chondroplasty.

The primary objective is to assess the feasibility of recruitment, acceptance of randomization, participant retention, completion of imaging and questionnaires, and adherence to the study procedures. Secondary objectives include exploring differences in ankle pain, function, healing on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), complications, and the need for additional surgery.

Participants will undergo postoperative rehabilitation according to standard clinical care and will be followed for up to 24 months after surgery.

The findings will help determine whether a larger multicentre randomized trial is feasible and provide preliminary information about healing and recovery following each surgical treatment. This pilot study is not designed to determine which treatment is more effective.
conditions: Osteochondritis Dissecans of Ankle and Joints of Foot
primary_outcomes: Recruitment Rate
title: Pediatric OCD Talus RCT Feasibility

brief_summary:
This study will assess whether reports generated by ZERO, a mobile system for interpreting electrocardiogram (ECG) images, improve clinicians' ability to identify causes of chest pain compared with interpretation without AI assistance.

A total of 120 licensed cardiology clinicians will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to ZERO-assisted or unassisted interpretation. Each clinician will assess 30 ECG cases during a single session lasting up to 60 minutes. The cases will include five examples from each of six diagnostic categories: unstable angina, non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, aortic dissection, pulmonary embolism, and other diagnoses. No case or patient will be repeated within or across clinicians.

For each case, clinicians will first review the ECG and submit an initial diagnosis that cannot subsequently be changed. Clinicians in the ZERO-assisted group will then view a fixed report generated before clinician randomization. Clinicians in the unassisted group will review the ECG again without an AI report. All clinicians will then submit a final diagnosis.

Diagnostic performance will be assessed against clinical reference diagnoses established before the interpretation task and withheld from participating clinicians. The study will use ECG cases from completed clinical encounters and will not affect patient care. The hypothesis is that ZERO-assisted clinicians will achieve higher final diagnostic accuracy than unassisted clinicians.
primary_outcomes: Finalfirst-choice diagnostic accuracy
title: AI Assistance for Clinicians Identifying Causes of Chest Pain From ECG Images

brief_summary: This is a single-center, Phase 1/2 clinical trial evaluating the safety, tolerability, RP2D, and preliminary efficacy of ZEN003694 in combination with RT in patients with metastatic UPS and MFS who have completed first- or second- line doxorubicin-based chemotherapy without disease progression.
primary_outcomes: Safety and Adverse Events (AEs)
title: SPARK UPS/MFS: Study Of BET Inhibition With ZEN003694 To Potentiate Anti-Tumor Responses With Radiotherapy To Kickstart Abscopal Effect In Metastatic Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma (UPS) And Myxofibrosarcoma (MFS).

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if tirzepatide, a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, helps to treat idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) when added to acetazolamide, which is the standard medical therapy for IIH. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does tirzepatide lower the mean daily acetazolamide dose at 12 months?
* Does tirzepatide add-on therapy improve the likelihood of remission of IIH, improve weight loss, reduce cumulative acetazolamide exposure, improve ophthalmic outcome measures, improve normalization of intracranial hypertension as measured by lumbar puncture (LP) opening pressure, improve headache and quality of life measures and, improve MRI findings of intracranial hypertension?

Investigators will compare tirzepatide to a placebo/sham injection in patients who are treated with a predefined dosing schedule of acetazolamide that adjusts based upon the response of papilledema and other IIH symptoms such as headache.

In addition to receiving treatment with acetazolamide, participants will:

* Receive weekly tirzepatide injections or a placebo/sham injection for 12 months, followed by 12 months of open-label observation.
* Attend clinic visits at enrollment and months 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, and 12 for neuro-ophthalmic examination and testing.
* During other months meet with investigator or research assistant by phone for symptom documentation and medication adjustment.
* Keep a record of any significant of days with headache for more than three hours or when a medication was taken for acute treatment of headache.
primary_outcomes: Mean daily acetazolamide dose at 12 months
title: Tirzepatide for the REduction of AceTazolamide in Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension

brief_summary: This single-center, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of tegileridine, a biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, in patients undergoing gastrointestinal endoscopy under sedation, compared with sufentanil. A total of 338 patients scheduled for gastrointestinal endoscopy under sedation were enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either tegileridine or sufentanil. The primary outcome is the incidence of respiratory depression. Secondary outcomes include the incidences of hypotension and postoperative nausea and vomiting, sedation success rate, supplemental propofol dose, procedure duration, recovery time, and patient satisfaction. This study will provide clinical evidence to support individualized and precision-based anesthesia strategies for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
conditions: Sedation and Anesthesia Management for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Respiratory Depression
title: Safety and Efficacy of Tegileridine in Painless Gastrointestinal Endoscopy

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluates the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on body composition, inflammatory biomarkers, and circulating microRNAs in adults with clinical obesity. Circulating microRNAs are small regulatory molecules that may reflect exercise-induced adaptations and inter-tissue communication related to skeletal muscle and metabolic health. The study investigates whether exercise-induced changes in adiposity are accompanied by changes in inflammatory status and circulating microRNA profiles associated with skeletal muscle adaptations and metabolic health.
primary_outcomes: Total Body Fat Mass Assessed by Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis
title: High-Intensity Interval Training, Inflammatory Biomarkers, and Circulating MicroRNAs in Human Clinical Obesity.

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to assess the actual temperature drop of medical gases from the distal end of the heated ventilator circuit to the tracheal carina during invasive mechanical ventilation with active humidification. This analysis reflects the investigators' intention to observe the temperature drop under real-world clinical practice conditions, while assessing potential interactions with patient body temperature, ambient temperature, and the size of unheated ventilatory connectors. These findings may provide insight into the appropriate temperature and humidity targets, thereby further optimizing active humidification during invasive mechanical ventilation.
conditions: Assess the Actual Temperature Drop of Medical Gases From the Distal End of the Heated Ventilator Circuit to the Tracheal Carina
lead_sponsor: Azienda Sanitaria Universitaria Integrata del Trentino
primary_outcomes: Temperature drop
title: Evaluation of the Temperature Difference of Medical Gases Between the Heated Inspiratory Limb and the Tracheal Carina in Patients Undergoing Invasive Mechanical Ventilation With Active Humidification: A Crossover Clinical Study.

brief_summary:
The present study seeks to develop the software function of Sleep Cycle's app to estimate risk of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) compared to polysomnography (PSG) in adults in an over-the-counter setting (i.e., home environment). The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. To develop the Sleep Cycle app's function to differentiate between subjects with a 'high risk of sleep apnea \[i.e., an Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) of 15 or more\]' vs subjects with 'low risk of sleep apnea \[i.e., AHI \< 15\], and
2. To develop an algorithm to distinguish between wake vs sleep, as well as classifying different sleep stages (ie, light sleep \[N1 and N2\] vs deep sleep \[N3\] vs Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep).

Researchers will compare Sleep Cycle's app to PSG (gold standard measure of diagnosing sleep apnea and measuring sleep stages) to see if Sleep Cycle's app can estimate the risk of sleep apnea.

Researchers will evaluate the sensitivity and specificity of the app to determine the research aims by comparing 2 groups: adults with an AHI \<15 and adults with an AHI of 15 or more.

Participants will:

Undertake one night of at-home PSG with 3x additional technologies: Sleep Cycle app on iPhone next to their bed + an audio recorder (both to record audio), and wear an Apple Watch to measure physiological measures (eg, heart rate).
primary_outcomes: AHI (Apnea-Hypopnea Index)
title: Development of the Sleep Cycle App's Tracking Abilities of Sleep and Sleep Behaviors

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Mini-RISK, a short group program at school, reduces anxiety in young people aged 12 to 16 more than the usual help they get from the school nurse.

The main question it aims to answer is:

Does Mini-RISK lower anxiety symptoms more than usual school nurse support, measured 8 weeks after the start?

Other questions are:

Does Mini-RISK improve quality of life, school attendance and school functioning? Does Mini-RISK reduce the ways families and schools help young people avoid what they fear (called accommodation)? Which young people benefit most, for example depending on how they handle uncertainty, how their family functions, bullying, and social media use?

About 70 schools in 10 municipalities in Agder, Norway, were assigned by chance (like drawing lots) to offer either Mini-RISK or usual school nurse support. Young people who seek help for anxiety at school get the help their school offers. Researchers will compare the two groups to see if Mini-RISK works better than usual support.

In Mini-RISK, groups of 4 to 6 young people meet at school for 8 sessions over 8 weeks (about 15.5 hours in total). The groups are led by a school nurse and a school social teacher who have been trained in the program. Parents take part in 4 sessions and contact teachers in 2. Young people learn about anxiety and practice, step by step, facing situations they fear, with support from parents and teachers.

Usual support means individual follow-up from the school nurse, such as supportive conversations, adjustments at school and referral to other services when needed.

Participants and their parents will:

Fill out online questionnaires at the start, after 8 weeks, after 22 weeks and after 12 months (about 15 to 20 minutes each time) Answer a short questionnaire (about 5 minutes) each week during the 8-week program period

After the randomized part of the study, schools that offered usual support will also be trained in Mini-RISK, and data from these schools will be used to study who benefits most from the program.
primary_outcomes: Change in Anxiety Symptoms (Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, Child Version, Total Score)
Change in Anxiety Symptoms (Spence Children's Anxiety Scale, Parent Version, Total Score)
title: Mini-RISK in Agder: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial of a Low-Threshold School-Based Program for Anxious Students Delivered by School Personnel in the School Setting

brief_summary:
Anaemia is common in pregnancy and can cause problems for both the mother and the baby. Iron tablets are an effective treatment, but many pregnant women do not take them regularly. Reasons include forgetfulness, side effects, and limited knowledge about anaemia.

This randomized controlled study evaluated whether giving pregnant women additional education about anaemia, on top of routine prenatal care, improves their awareness of anaemia, their regular use of iron supplements, and their haemoglobin levels.

Pregnant women aged 18 to 45 years, between 16 and 34 weeks of pregnancy and diagnosed with anaemia, were randomly assigned to one of three groups:

Group 1: routine information + an anaemia awareness brochure + an antenatal education class Group 2: routine information + an anaemia awareness brochure only Group 3 (control): routine information only

Anaemia awareness, iron supplement use, and haemoglobin levels were assessed at the start of the study and after 4 weeks. Haemoglobin levels after delivery were also recorded.

The main question of the study was whether haemoglobin levels after 4 weeks differ among the three groups. The study also examined whether education and brochures increase women's knowledge about anaemia and help them take iron supplements more regularly.
primary_outcomes: Haemoglobin Level at 4 Weeks
Change in Anaemia Awareness Score
Adherence to Oral Iron Supplementation
title: Antenatal Education and Brochures to Improve Anaemia Awareness and Iron Use in Pregnant Women

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether high-flow oxygen therapy (HFOT) is more effective than conventional oxygen therapy (COT) in reducing episodes of intraoperative oxygen desaturation (oxygen saturation \[SpO2\] ≤ 90%) during colonoscopy under general anesthesia in adults with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² or higher.

The main question it aims to answer is:

Does high-flow oxygen therapy reduce the occurrence of intraoperative oxygen desaturation compared with conventional oxygen therapy during colonoscopy under general anesthesia? Researchers will compare high-flow oxygen therapy with conventional oxygen therapy to determine whether high-flow oxygen therapy reduces the occurrence of intraoperative oxygen desaturation.

Participants will:

Be screened during their anesthesia consultation between 60 days and 48 hours before the scheduled colonoscopy.

Be randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either conventional oxygen therapy or high-flow oxygen therapy. Receive standard monitoring and 3 minutes of pre-oxygenation according to their assigned treatment group.

Undergo colonoscopy under general anesthesia while breathing spontaneously. Be monitored for oxygen desaturation during the procedure. Have ventilatory and hemodynamic data recorded during the procedure and collected immediately after the colonoscopy.

The study will include adults scheduled for a colonoscopy at Bichat-Claude Bernard Hospital, Beaujon Hospital, or Louis Mourier Hospital.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with at least one episode of oxygen desaturation (SpO2 ≤ 90%) during the procedure
title: High-flow Nasal Oxygenation in Obese Patients During Colonoscopy: a Randomized Controlled Trial (COCOON)

brief_summary:
Induction of labor is a common procedure used to start labor when delivery is recommended. The process may involve cervical ripening, which helps prepare the cervix for labor. This period can be associated with anxiety and discomfort for pregnant patients. Music therapy may help reduce anxiety and improve the experience of care during this process.

The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether a 45-minute individualized music therapy session could reduce anxiety among patients undergoing cervical ripening as part of labor induction. The study was conducted at Meir Medical Center, a tertiary hospital in Kfar Saba, Israel.

A total of 102 patients with singleton term pregnancies who were undergoing cervical ripening with a vaginal Cervidil pessary participated in the study. Patients were assigned to either a music therapy group or a control group according to the availability of a music therapist. The music therapy group received an individualized 45-minute session delivered by a certified music therapist, while the control group received standard obstetric care without a music therapy session.

Anxiety, pain, and salivary cortisol levels (a measure of the body's stress response) were assessed before and after the intervention. The researchers compared the changes in these measurements between the two groups to evaluate whether music therapy was associated with reduced anxiety and stress during cervical ripening.
primary_outcomes: State Anxiety (STAI-S)
Salivary Cortisol
Subjective Anxiety Score
Pain Intensity (VAS)
title: Music Therapy for Anxiety Reduction During Cervical Ripening

brief_summary:
This study will compare two nerve block techniques for pain relief after total laparoscopic hysterectomy, a minimally invasive operation to remove the uterus. Both techniques involve injecting a local anesthetic near muscles of the lower back, but the injections are given at different depths.

Women aged 18 to 65 years who are scheduled for this surgery will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: erector spinae plane block, deep erector spinae plane block, or no nerve block. The nerve blocks will be performed on both sides of the lower back after surgery. All participants will receive standard pain medication.

The main aim is to compare pain scores one hour after surgery. The study will also assess pain during the first 24 hours, opioid pain medication use, the time until additional pain relief is needed, nausea and vomiting, time to hospital discharge, patient satisfaction, and quality of recovery.
primary_outcomes: Pain Intensity at Rest at 1 Hour After Block Administration
title: Erector Spinae Plane Blocks for Pain Control After Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to learn about the safety of a new medicine called IPN60350 and how the body responds to it. Researchers will also look for early signs of antitumor activity in adults with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors.

All participants in this study will receive IPN60350, either alone or in combination with other anticancer therapies.

The study has two parts.

* Phase Ia (dose escalation) will test IPN60350 at different dose levels to learn which doses are safe and can be given in future parts of the study.
* Phase Ib (dose optimization and expansion) will test one or more selected dose levels in a larger number of participants. This will help researchers better understand the safety of IPN60350 and whether it shows early signs of antitumor activity in different tumor types.

Each part will consist of the following periods:

* A screening period (up to 28 days) to assess whether the participant can take part, requiring at least 1 visit to the study center.
* A treatment period where IPN60350 is administered in repeating treatment cycles.

The study includes health assessments, blood tests, tissue samples (biopsies), and imaging scans to help researchers better understand the safety of IPN60350 and its potential effects on tumors.
primary_outcomes: Phase Ia: Percentage of Participants With Dose Limiting Toxicities (DLTs)
Phase Ia and Ib: Percentage of Participants Experiencing Treatment Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) and Treatment Emergent Serious Adverse Events (TESAEs)
Phase Ib: Objective Response Rate (ORR)
Phase Ib: Percentage of Participants With Dose Interruptions and Permanent Treatment Discontinuations
title: A Phase I/II Study to Learn About the Safety and Effects of a New Medicine Called IPN60350 Alone or in Combination With Other Anticancer Therapies in Adults With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors

brief_summary: The main purpose of this trial is to find out whether BHB-1893 works better than placebo in adults with non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM).

title: Acupuncture Delivery In The Clinical Decision Unit (CDU) For The Management Of Pain, Nausea, And Other Symptoms

brief_summary:
The aim of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of a low-volume static stretching program in improving posterior chain flexibility in young professional football players. The primary research question is whether performing 120 seconds of static stretching per week for 6 weeks is sufficient to improve posterior chain flexibility compared with no stretching intervention.

The study will be conducted as a two-arm randomized controlled trial. Male professional football players aged 17-19 years will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either a static stretching group or a control group. The intervention will last 6 weeks. The stretching group will perform one supervised stretching session per week, consisting of two 60-second sets of static stretching targeting the posterior chain, separated by a 45-second rest interval. Stretching will be performed at high intensity, defined as the maximal tolerable level of discomfort. The control group will not perform any additional stretching intervention.

Posterior chain flexibility will be assessed before and after the intervention using a modified stand-and-reach test. Each participant will complete two trials, and the mean value will be used for analysis. The post-intervention assessment will be performed by an assessor blinded to group allocation.
lead_sponsor: Józef Piłsudski University of Physical Education
primary_outcomes: Flexibility - stand and reach test
title: Effects of Low-Volume Static Stretching on Posterior Chain Flexibility in Professional Football Players

brief_summary:
This prospective observational study aims to describe and characterize the multidimensional care needs of children and adolescents aged 1 month to 18 years with rare genetic and metabolic diseases, with particular emphasis on the identification of pediatric palliative care needs.

The study seeks to answer the question of which clinical, physical, psychological, social, and care-related needs characterize this population, and to what extent these needs are associated with complex care requirements and potential eligibility for pediatric palliative care.

Additional objectives include assessing pain, sleep disturbances, psychological well-being, quality of life, physical and social functioning, medication-related adverse events, symptom interference with daily life, and caregiver burden. The study will also explore individual care needs and the transition from pediatric to adult healthcare services.

A subgroup of approximately 150 participants will undergo longitudinal assessments every three months for up to 12 months to describe changes in care needs over time and identify factors potentially associated with worsening clinical and care complexity. Furthermore, a qualitative substudy involving caregivers and adolescents will explore the lived experience of illness and the meaning attributed to the disease by children and their families through semi-structured interviews.

Overall, the study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the care needs and illness experience of children with rare genetic and metabolic diseases, supporting the early identification of complex needs and the development of more personalized, proactive, and family-centered care pathways.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS San Gerardo dei Tintori
primary_outcomes: AccaPed Total Score for the Assessment of Complex Pediatric Palliative Care Needs
title: Healthcare Needs and Illness Experience in Children With Rare Genetic and Metabolic Diseases

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to test whether a Mediterranean-style diet and a time-restricted eating plan ("intermittent fasting") are easy to follow and acceptable for people who were recently diagnosed with kidney cancer.

brief_summary:
This study tests a new way to give an antibiotic to older adults with pneumonia. Pneumonia is a lung infection.

Piperacillin-tazobactam is an antibiotic. Doctors often use it to treat pneumonia in older adults. Right now, doctors usually give this drug every 8 hours. They let it drip into the vein over 3 hours.

But early research suggests a different schedule may work better. This study will test giving the drug every 6 hours. The drip will last 4 hours. Researchers think this may help the drug fight germs better.

The study will compare the usual schedule with the new schedule. Participants will join one of two groups. One group will get the usual schedule. The other group will get the new schedule.

Researchers will check how well the drug works. They will also watch for side effects. They want to find the safest and most helpful way to give this drug.

Adults aged 65 and older with community-acquired pneumonia can join. Community-acquired pneumonia is a lung infection that starts outside of a hospital.
interventions: Piperacillin Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (Bangda®)
Piperacillin Sodium and Tazobactam Sodium for Injection (Bangda®)
primary_outcomes: The proportion of patients achieving the predefined pharmacodynamic (PD) target.
title: A Superiority Study of Model-Guided Optimized Dosing Versus Empirical Dosing of Piperacillin/Tazobactam in the Treatment of Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Elderly Patients

brief_summary: Background: Non traumatic Emergency general surgery disease are responsible for significant morbidity and mortality. In clinical practice a good number of deaths could probably be avoided. This may be related to delayed clinical decisions, imaging, or laboratory diagnostic inaccuracy. Objective: The ANUBI Registry aims to analyze avoidable deaths in non traumatic emergency general diseases evaluating all risk factors. Methods: ANUBI is a multicenter, prospective, registry carried out across multiple continents. Adult patients admitted and died for non traumatic emergency general surgery disease will be included. Data collection will be focused on all medical, surgical, radiologic, laboratory informations. Results The primary outcome is the incidence of avoidable death. Secondary outcomes include all possible factors affecting related decision-making and preventability of death. Conclusions: ANUBI aims globally assess preventable deaths in non traumatic emergency general surgery diseases analyzing potentially practice changing factors to patients' outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Avoidable and Probably Avoidable Deaths Following Non-Traumatic Emergency General Surgery
title: Avoidable Deaths After Non Traumatic Emergency General Surgery Registry

brief_summary: This study investigated how a single session of moderate-intensity exercise performed on land or in water affects working memory in physically active young men. Working memory is the ability to temporarily hold and use information, which is important for everyday activities. Participants completed two exercise sessions on separate days, one on land and one in water, with at least 48 hours between sessions. Each session involved 20 minutes of stepping exercise at a moderate intensity. Working memory was assessed using a computerized 2-back task before and after exercise in the same environment in which the exercise was performed. The study compared changes in working memory performance between the land and water conditions, including the number of correct responses, incorrect responses, and response times.
primary_outcomes: Change in Working Memory Accuracy (Correct Target Responses)
title: Acute Effects of Land-Based and Water-Based Exercise on Working Memory

brief_summary:
The treatment of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) requires movement of the head through several positions. This is known as the particle repositioning manoeuvre or the Epley manoeuvre. Getting this manoeuvre right helps to dislodge debris from the inner ear that might cause the dizziness. The investigators have developed a head sensing device and particle repositioning manoeuvre application designed to support a healthcare professional to perform these movements and treat the condition.

Here the investigators are aiming to see if, with the help of the investigational device and app, a non-specialist (such as an ENT nurse, or a GP doctor) can perform the particle repositioning manoeuvre as well as an ENT specialist can.

The investigators hope that in the future this would allow patients with BPPV to be treated well by a non-specialist and so reduce the waiting times for this treatment manoeuvre.

The investigators aim to validate and assess the utility of a head position sensing device, and a PRM application (App) that will support healthcare professionals perform the manoeuvre.
lead_sponsor: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
primary_outcomes: To identify patient improvement using Dizziness Handicap Inventory Questionnaire and Novel HEADSPIN BPPV Symptom Questionnaire taken before and after using the HEADSPIN device
title: HEAD Position Sensing for the Particle Repositioning Maneuver Technique IN Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo: a Validation and Feasibility Study

brief_summary: This study describes only the Aim 2 clinical trial component of the NIH-funded project "Adapting an Intervention to Reduce Stigma among MSM and Healthcare Providers in Vietnam". The purpose of this pilot randomized waitlist-controlled trial (N=180) is to evaluate the preliminary efficacy of DONGHANH, a stigma-reduction intervention for men who have sex with men and healthcare providers in Vietnam. The study will provide preliminary data on the intervention's potential impact to inform the design of a larger future trial evaluating its effects on HIV prevention and care outcomes in Vietnam and in other countries with collectivist cultures.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of the intervention
Acceptability of of the intervention
Appropriateness of the intervention
title: Stigma Reduction Intervention for MSM and Healthcare Providers

brief_summary:
Tumor dosimetry for meningiomas is substantially lower (7 to 8 times lower) than for neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), even though the injected activities are identical for both indications.

The hypothesis of this study is that organs at risk receive a higher absorbed dose in the case of meningiomas than with NETs.

A literature review has supported this hypothesis; therefore, it is appropriate to verify it through this retrospective study.
primary_outcomes: To compare the dosimetry of organs at risk in patients treated with Lutathera® for meningioma versus neuroendocrine tumor
title: Dosimetry of Organs at Risk for Lutathera Treatment Between Meningioma and Neuroendocrine Tumor

brief_summary: This study is a single - center, single - arm, open - label, single - dose, dose - escalation exploratory study. The main purpose is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of autologous tumor - infiltrating lymphocyte injection in the treatment of recurrent or metastatic lung cancer or cervical cancer. Meanwhile, it will also preliminarily explore the effectiveness, PK characteristics, PD characteristics and changes in immune - related parameters of autologous tumor - infiltrating lymphocyte injection in subjects with recurrent or metastatic lung cancer or cervical cancer.
conditions: Recurrent or Metastatic Lung Cancer or Cervical Cancer
primary_outcomes: ORR
title: Exploratory Clinical Study of Autologous Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes (TIL) Injection

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study will investigate the effects of an Akkermansia muciniphila-based probiotic supplement, Panthea Core, on autonomic and vascular function in postmenopausal women with hypertension.

Up to 60 participants aged 45 to 65 years will be enrolled to obtain approximately 40 evaluable datasets. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive Panthea Core or a matched placebo capsule daily for 12 weeks.

The study will evaluate safety, tolerability, menopausal symptoms, and changes in autonomic and vascular physiology. The primary mechanistic outcome is muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA), measured using microneurography. Secondary physiological outcomes include heart rate variability, baroreflex sensitivity, endothelial function assessed by flow-mediated dilation, and blood pressure.

Additional assessments will include sleep, menopausal symptoms, mood, cognitive function, circulating metabolic markers, and gut microbiome composition. Participants will complete baseline and post-intervention assessments, with additional safety monitoring throughout supplementation and approximately one month after the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Muscle Sympathetic Nerve Activity (MSNA)
Incidence of Adverse Events
Change in Comprehensive Metabolic Panel Laboratory Measures
Supplement Adherence
Study Retention
title: Effects of Akkermansia Muciniphila-Based Probiotics on Autonomic and Vascular Function

brief_summary: This randomized phase 2 study evaluates the efficacy and safety of nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab plus cabozantinib as first-line treatment in patients with metastatic TFE-rearranged renal cell carcinoma. Patients are randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups. Following disease progression, patients receive protocol-specified second-line treatment with lenvatinib plus everolimus. The study assesses treatment outcomes during first-line therapy and across the planned treatment sequence.
primary_outcomes: First-Line Objective Response Rate (ORR)
title: First-Line Nivolumab Plus Ipilimumab or Cabozantinib Followed by Second-Line Lenvatinib Plus Everolimus in Metastatic TFE-Rearranged Renal Cell Carcinoma

brief_summary:
This study tested whether a smartphone app could help university students with overweight or obesity manage their weight. It also looked at changes in body measurements, physical activity, and related health behaviors.

The study asked three main questions:

Did students who used the app manage their weight better than students who received a leaflet? Did the app affect waist size, body fat, or how physically active students were? Did the app affect what students knew, believed, and did about weight management or how they rated their quality of life?

The study included students aged 18 to 25 from Hanoi Medical University and the Banking Academy in Hanoi, Vietnam. The researchers randomly assigned students to two groups:

App group. Students used an app that gave them advice on eating and exercise... They could use the app to track what they ate and how active they were.

Leaflet group. Students received a leaflet about healthy eating and physical activity for weight management at the start of the study.

The researchers followed both groups for six months. They measured students' weight, waist size, and body fat. Students also answered questions about their physical activity, eating habits, and quality of life.

brief_summary:
This study will test whether adding thread embedding acupuncture to an antihistamine helps adults with chronic hives whose symptoms remain bothersome despite taking the antihistamine. In thread embedding acupuncture, a clinician uses a needle to place a small dissolvable thread at an acupuncture point. The comparison procedure uses the same acupuncture points and a needle, without placing a thread. Both groups take cetirizine.

The researchers plan to enroll 124 adults at three hospitals in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of the two groups. They will receive two procedures, two weeks apart. Participants and the people who assess their symptoms will not know which procedure they received. The main assessment compares changes in hives and itching after four weeks. The study will also assess quality of life, a blood marker called total immunoglobulin E, additional antihistamine use, side effects, and whether symptoms return during follow-up through week 8.
lead_sponsor: University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in 7-Day Urticaria Activity Score (UAS7) at Week 4
title: Thread Embedding Acupuncture Added to Antihistamine Treatment for Chronic Urticaria

brief_summary:
Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the axial skeleton that commonly leads to restricted spinal mobility, postural deformities such as thoracic hyperkyphosis, and reduced chest wall expansion, which can impair respiratory function and quality of life. Exercise is the cornerstone of rehabilitation in AS, and manual therapy techniques may provide additional benefit by restoring mobility of the thoracic cage and shoulder girdle.

The aim of this randomized controlled, single-blind trial is to investigate whether scapular mobilization added to a conventional exercise program improves chest expansion and respiratory function (primary outcomes), as well as pain, disease activity, function, spinal mobility, posture, exercise capacity, and quality of life (secondary outcomes) in patients with AS. Thirty-four patients will be randomly allocated to either scapular mobilization plus conventional exercise or conventional exercise alone, 3 sessions per week for 8 weeks (24 sessions). Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, after treatment (week 8), and at month 3.
primary_outcomes: Chest Expansion
Forced Vital Capacity (FVC)
Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second (FEV1)
FEV1/FVC Ratio
title: Scapular Mobilization Added to Conventional Exercise in Ankylosing Spondylitis

brief_summary:
This clinical investigation evaluates the Ambu Broncho AI Navigator, an investigational software system designed to provide real-time navigational support during bronchoscopy. The system uses artificial intelligence to identify and display airway anatomy during procedures and to help bronchoscopists track which airway segments have been examined.

The study is conducted at Odense University Hospital and consists of two phases. In Phase 2a, experienced bronchoscopists use the system during routine bronchoscopies to evaluate and optimize technical settings and usability. For this phase 45 patients will be enrolled. In Phase 2b, bronchoscopies are randomized (1:1) to be performed with or without the Broncho AI Navigator to evaluate the impact of AI guidance on procedural performance. For this phase 108 patients will be enrolled.

Adult patients undergoing elective bronchoscopy are enrolled, while the primary study subjects are the bronchoscopists performing the procedures. The study evaluates whether use of the Broncho AI Navigator improves bronchoscopy performance by increasing diagnostic completeness, improving structured progression through the bronchial tree, and reducing procedure time. The findings will support further development and future validation of the Broncho AI Navigator in clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic completeness
Structured progression
Procedure time
title: AI-Guided Bronchoscopy Using the Broncho AI Navigator

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can text messages sent during the two weeks after the lab visit help people who drink alcohol have fewer suicidal thoughts and behaviors, compared with getting no text messages?

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn if automated pupillometry (AP)-a simple tool that measures how the eye responds to a brief light stimulus-can help diagnose diabetic retinopathy (DR), a complication of diabetes that can lead to blindness, in people with type 2 diabetes (T2DM).

The main question it aims to answer is:

• How accurate is AP for screening DR in people with T2DM?

DR usually has no symptoms in its early stages, so early screening is crucial to prevent progression to blindness. Participants in this study will undergo two tests:

* AP, which measures the eye's response to light.
* A fundoscopic examination (FE), which is the current test used to diagnose DR. FE is performed by an ophthalmologist, making it more expensive and harder to access due to long waiting lists. These challenges mean not all people with diabetes can have this test annually, as recommended. AP could offer a cheaper and more accessible option that doesn't require a specialist, potentially reducing waiting times and enabling earlier diagnosis of DR in people with diabetes.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of automated pupillometry (AP) for diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening
title: Automated Pupillometry for Diabetic Retinopathy Screening
